jobs.title: SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST) Fire & Landscape Ecologist
jobs.description:
Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) (Fire & Landscape Ecologist) 

CA Coastal Commission 

$8,055.00 - $11,269.00 per Month New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable. 

Final Filing Date: 12/1/2026 

The California Coastal Commission is seeking two Senior Environmental Scientists (Specialists) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its offices in San Francisco, Santa Cruz, or Long Beach. These positions will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological health and restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, woodlands, shrublands, grasslands, and wetlands throughout California's coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas. It is anticipated that one position will focus on the northern portion of the state, and the other on the southern. 

The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast's sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Under the direction of the Ecology Team Manager, the successful incumbents will be integrated into the existing team of six ecologists and work with Commission staff to address ecological issues raised in the Commission's policy, planning, and regulatory work as relates to wildfire resilience and risk reduction efforts. This work will focus on understanding and addressing the ecological effects of vegetation management for fuel reduction and wildfire resilience, including through ecological restoration, throughout California's coastal zone. It will necessitate cooperation with other scientific and technical teams such as Mapping and Water Quality, coordination with the Commission's Statewide Planning Unit, and provision of scientific support to staff and the Commission. It will also involve programmatic coordination to streamline natural resource protection along infrastructure corridors associated with utilities and transit. Generally, the incumbents will be expected to: review and analyze proposals, including for expedited wildfire mitigation efforts, and a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act, relevant certified plans (e.g., Local Coastal Plans, Public Works Plans), and Environmental Protection Plans. 

Key functions of the job include: analyzing proposed fire resilience and risk reduction work for consistency with applicable Coastal Act policies and/or standards associated with applicable Environmental Protection Plans; tracking topical scientific literature including white papers and peer-reviewed publications; guiding related policy based on scientific understanding of the issues and existing frameworks; developing recommendations on how to avoid and minimize adverse impacts to native habitat (including for communities and species) associated with fuel reduction and vegetation management efforts across the landscape while advancing ecological resilience; contributing to the development of recommendations for Commission regulatory action, including advisories, staff reports, permit conditions, and planning documents; communicating with project proponents; updating and maintaining a spatial database of authorized fire resilience and risk reduction work and conducting geospatial analyses; reviewing monitoring and mitigation plans and reports; conducting site visits and inspections to evaluate on-the-ground ecological conditions; writing technical memoranda to support and accompany staff reports and recommendations; and providing technical presentations at public meetings. The incumbents may also represent the Commission staff on multi-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public. 

These positions offer considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California's coastal landscape. 

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement. 

Guided by the California Coastal Act of 1976, the California Coastal Commission is a small state agency responsible for protecting and enhancing California's coast and ocean resources. It does so through careful planning and regulation of environmentally-sustainable development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast, rigorous use of science, strong public participation, education, and effective intergovernmental coordination. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone. 

The California Coastal Commission values diversity at all levels of the organization and is committed to fostering an environment in which employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. General Description

The primary responsibilities of this position involve inspection and enforcement of state and local environmental health laws, rules and regulations that apply to food services, lodging, institutions and day care centers.

Duties And Responsibilities

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this position. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the position as necessary.

Perform State mandated, unannounced sanitation inspections of Food, Lodging, and Institution, Childcare and Tattoo facilities.
Investigate complaints from the public, medical referrals and community illness reports concerning suspected violations of environmental laws, rules and regulations.
Complete and maintain necessary records of these inspections and/or complaint investigations.
Conduct consultative visits with current, or potential, establishment owners/operators to build rapport as well as to educate on Environmental Health requirements.
Take appropriate permit action when facilities fail to comply with minimum sanitation standards, and/or when an imminent health hazard exists.
Perform office duties involving correspondence with the public.
Collect routine water samples for all regulated facilities.
Provide field training for new employees and other public health personnel.
Participate in educational programs that are required to retain REHS status (minimum 15 hours of continuing education per year).
Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Working knowledge of environmental health laws, rules, and procedures, as well as a complete understanding of the concepts of public heath law.
Practical knowledge of microbiology, biology, chemistry, food science, epidemiology, soil science, entomology, and basic engineering technology as applied to environmental health practices.
General knowledge of community resources.
Working knowledge of the responsibilities of other agencies involved in environmental health work.
Working knowledge of inspection methods and investigation techniques as applied in environmental health.
Ability to analyze and comprehend a wide variety of technical and administrative regulations, records, and reports.
Ability to develop and express ideas and opinions concisely, comprehensively, and clearly in oral and written from.
Ability to independently plan and schedule work activities.
Ability to apply environmental health knowledge and techniques in the investigation of environmental health problems.
Ability to exercise sound judgment and deal tactfully with clients while enforcing public health laws is a must.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team is essential.
Effective oral and written communication skills highly desired.
Computer use is essential with working knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite.

Minimum Education And Experience Requirements

Graduation from a four-year college or university with 30 semester of course work in the physical or biological sciences and two years of exposure in environmental health; or a four-year or Master’s degree in environmental health from a program which is accredited by the National Accreditation Council for Environmental Health Curricula of the National Environmental Health Association and one year of experience in environmental health.

Special Note

Must be able to enter a correctional facility.
This is a generalized representation of positions in this class and is not intended to identify essential functions per ADA. Examples of work are primarily essential functions of the majority of positions, but may not be applicable to all positions.
Appointees must be eligible and apply for registration as an Environmental Health Specialist Intern within 60 days of employment.
Appointees may remain registered as an Environmental Health Specialist Intern until registration as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist or up to two years, whichever comes first.

Special Certifications And Licenses Requirements

Must be a Registered Environmental Health Specialist in North Carolina .
Must possess a valid North Carolina driver's license with a three-year acceptable driving record.

Preffered Qualifications

Registered Environmental Health Specialist candidates with current State authorizations in food and lodging are preferred.
Bilingual skills (Spanish) desired.

Required

To further the mission of the Durham County Department of Public Health (DCoDPH) to partner with our community to advance health equity, protect the environment, and promote health and wellness for all , DCoDPH is implementing the employee vaccination and tuberculosis screening policies. All DCoDPH employees are considered healthcare personnel (HCP) working in a health care setting with the potential for exposure to patients and/or infectious materials and, therefore, are required to comply and provide documented proof of the following:

Measles, Mumps & Rubella (MMR) vaccination/immunity
Varicella-Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) vaccination/immunity

Identified DCoDPH HCP with potential Bloodborne Pathogen (BBP) exposure have an additional requirement for the Hepatitis B vaccination. Required vaccination, serological testing to determine immunity, and baseline tuberculosis screening are available for all Public Health employees who elect to become DCoDPH patients upon request and at no cost.

Proof of vaccination and tuberculosis screening must be provided to Human Resources within seven (7) business days prior to the date of employment.

jobs.title: Intermediate Permitting Specialist - Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Intermediate Permitting Specialist

Play an integral role in Worley Consulting’s Environmental & Sustainability (E&S) team, helping energy sector clients navigate environmental permitting and regulatory requirements while supporting the responsible development and delivery of complex projects across the United States.

You will work alongside experienced environmental practitioners, engineers and project professionals on projects spanning upstream, midstream and downstream energy, as well as emerging markets such as hydrogen, carbon capture, renewable power and biofuels. This is an opportunity to strengthen your technical expertise, gain meaningful client and regulatory exposure, and build your consulting career within a collaborative global organization.

Purpose of the role

As an Intermediate Permitting Specialist, you will support the planning, preparation and delivery of environmental permitting and regulatory solutions for energy and infrastructure projects.

You will help identify permitting requirements, prepare applications and technical documentation, maintain permit schedules and compliance requirements, and support engagement with clients, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders. Working with senior consultants and technical specialists, you will develop practical regulatory strategies that align environmental requirements with project objectives, schedules and delivery priorities.

The role offers a strong development pathway for an environmental professional who wants to deepen their permitting expertise, expand their client-facing capabilities and contribute to Worley Consulting’s continued growth in established and emerging energy markets.

Location(s)

This is a full-time, hybrid position based near a Worley U.S. office.

Desired locations: Houston TX, Long Beach or Monrovia CA, Chicago IL, Charleston WV, or Reading PA.

You will be collaborating with colleagues, clients and project teams across multiple locations. Travel to client meetings, regulatory engagements and project or field locations will be required based on project needs.

You Will Be Responsible For

Support environmental permitting, regulatory and advisory services for energy and infrastructure projects.
Identify federal, state and local permitting requirements and help develop strategies aligned with project objectives and schedules.
Prepare compliant permit applications, supporting technical studies, regulatory documentation and approval packages.
Support environmental permitting and reviews under NEPA, CEQA and other applicable federal, state and local frameworks.
Develop and maintain permit matrices, tracking tools, schedules and compliance databases to track regulatory milestones, permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
Prepare and review accurate, high-quality technical correspondence, environmental reports, work plans, project documentation, cost estimates and schedules.
Collaborate with senior environmental professionals, engineers and project teams to integrate permitting into multidisciplinary project planning and execution.
Engage with regulators, clients and project stakeholders, developing communication and consulting skills to support successful project outcomes.
Support project management by coordinating assigned tasks and tracking scope, schedule, budget and progress.
Support proposals, scope development, cost estimates and opportunity identification.
Support quality assurance and alignment with Worley’s E&S systems, technical standards and HSE expectations.
Participate in client meetings and field programs, traveling as needed for effective project delivery.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

You will bring a foundation in environmental permitting or regulatory consulting combined with strong technical writing, analytical and collaboration skills. You will be motivated to expand your expertise and take on increasing responsibility as part of multidisciplinary project teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology or a related discipline.
Typically 3–7 years of relevant experience, preferably in environmental consulting, engineering or regulation.
Working knowledge of U.S. environmental permitting, including NEPA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Familiarity with federal regulations, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Understanding of environmental compliance and permitting, including air and/or water requirements.
Experience supporting environmental permitting and preparing accurate, organized technical and regulatory documentation.
Demonstrated ability to track assigned project scope, schedules and budgets and identify potential variances.
Strong technical writing, reporting and documentation skills focused on quality, accuracy and detail.
Developing client-facing and stakeholder engagement skills; effective communication with clients, regulators and project teams.
Strong communication and collaboration skills for effective multidisciplinary teamwork.
Commitment to health, safety, environmental stewardship and responsible project delivery.
Motivation to build technical and consulting skills with guidance from experienced practitioners.

Additional Preferred Experience

Air quality permitting support experience and exposure to emissions modeling or regulatory strategy development.
Familiarity with CEQA and California environmental permitting requirements.
Exposure to environmental engineering, including stormwater management and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) planning.
Experience supporting proposals, cost estimates or project planning.
Experience or demonstrated interest in emerging energy sectors, including hydrogen, carbon capture and management, renewable power and biofuels.

Compensation

For California applicants

Salary Range: $85,398 - $113,821; based upon experience
Benefits: eligible for PTO, 401k, medical, vision, dental, etc.

Los Angeles

We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles' Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

Application of the pay band: Variation in salary is determined by factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.

Benefits

Feel the energy at Worley with access to a range of benefits including paid time off, holiday pay (usually 8 per year in the US), and eligibility to participate in the medical, life, dental, and vision insurance plans, as well as 401K plan.

Apply today

Bring your environmental permitting experience, curiosity and collaborative approach to a role where you can contribute to meaningful projects while continuing to develop as a trusted environmental professional.

You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners, work across multidisciplinary teams, gain exposure to clients and regulators, and broaden your experience across established and emerging energy markets. As your expertise develops, you will have opportunities to take on greater technical, project delivery and client responsibilities.

About Us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today’s needs and transition to more sustainable solutions. Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.

Moving forward together

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We’re building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it. We’re reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today’s low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

HDR has an exciting leadership opportunity for a Drinking Water Treatment Business Class Leader for the South Central Region that includes Texas, Louisiana, and Oklahoma. The Regional Drinking Water Treatment Business Class Leader will collaborate with area water business group managers, area market sector leaders, business class leaders, project managers, national business class lead and subject matter experts, and business development teams to support the growth and development of our drinking water treatment practice. Active participation in national practice groups related to drinking water treatment within HDR and active participation in National and Regional Drinking Water Professional Organizations. The ideal candidate will possess strong leadership and technical skills to oversee the large drinking water treatment projects in the South Central Region of the US while providing guidance and mentorship to junior, mid-level, and senior engineers.

Primary Responsibilities

In the role of Regional Drinking Water Treatment Business Class Leader, we’ll count on you to:

Provide key leadership with strategic drinking water clients in the South Central Region via technical workshops, professional organization involvement including conferences, and serving as client manager and project manager as needed.

jobs.title: Intermediate Permitting Specialist - Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Intermediate Permitting Specialist

Play an integral role in Worley Consulting’s Environmental & Sustainability (E&S) team, helping energy sector clients navigate environmental permitting and regulatory requirements while supporting the responsible development and delivery of complex projects across the United States.

You will work alongside experienced environmental practitioners, engineers and project professionals on projects spanning upstream, midstream and downstream energy, as well as emerging markets such as hydrogen, carbon capture, renewable power and biofuels. This is an opportunity to strengthen your technical expertise, gain meaningful client and regulatory exposure, and build your consulting career within a collaborative global organization.

Purpose of the role

As an Intermediate Permitting Specialist, you will support the planning, preparation and delivery of environmental permitting and regulatory solutions for energy and infrastructure projects.

You will help identify permitting requirements, prepare applications and technical documentation, maintain permit schedules and compliance requirements, and support engagement with clients, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders. Working with senior consultants and technical specialists, you will develop practical regulatory strategies that align environmental requirements with project objectives, schedules and delivery priorities.

The role offers a strong development pathway for an environmental professional who wants to deepen their permitting expertise, expand their client-facing capabilities and contribute to Worley Consulting’s continued growth in established and emerging energy markets.

Location(s)

This is a full-time, hybrid position based near a Worley U.S. office.

Desired locations: Houston TX, Long Beach or Monrovia CA, Chicago IL, Charleston WV, or Reading PA.

You will be collaborating with colleagues, clients and project teams across multiple locations. Travel to client meetings, regulatory engagements and project or field locations will be required based on project needs.

You Will Be Responsible For

Support environmental permitting, regulatory and advisory services for energy and infrastructure projects.
Identify federal, state and local permitting requirements and help develop strategies aligned with project objectives and schedules.
Prepare compliant permit applications, supporting technical studies, regulatory documentation and approval packages.
Support environmental permitting and reviews under NEPA, CEQA and other applicable federal, state and local frameworks.
Develop and maintain permit matrices, tracking tools, schedules and compliance databases to track regulatory milestones, permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
Prepare and review accurate, high-quality technical correspondence, environmental reports, work plans, project documentation, cost estimates and schedules.
Collaborate with senior environmental professionals, engineers and project teams to integrate permitting into multidisciplinary project planning and execution.
Engage with regulators, clients and project stakeholders, developing communication and consulting skills to support successful project outcomes.
Support project management by coordinating assigned tasks and tracking scope, schedule, budget and progress.
Support proposals, scope development, cost estimates and opportunity identification.
Support quality assurance and alignment with Worley’s E&S systems, technical standards and HSE expectations.
Participate in client meetings and field programs, traveling as needed for effective project delivery.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

You will bring a foundation in environmental permitting or regulatory consulting combined with strong technical writing, analytical and collaboration skills. You will be motivated to expand your expertise and take on increasing responsibility as part of multidisciplinary project teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology or a related discipline.
Typically 3–7 years of relevant experience, preferably in environmental consulting, engineering or regulation.
Working knowledge of U.S. environmental permitting, including NEPA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Familiarity with federal regulations, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Understanding of environmental compliance and permitting, including air and/or water requirements.
Experience supporting environmental permitting and preparing accurate, organized technical and regulatory documentation.
Demonstrated ability to track assigned project scope, schedules and budgets and identify potential variances.
Strong technical writing, reporting and documentation skills focused on quality, accuracy and detail.
Developing client-facing and stakeholder engagement skills; effective communication with clients, regulators and project teams.
Strong communication and collaboration skills for effective multidisciplinary teamwork.
Commitment to health, safety, environmental stewardship and responsible project delivery.
Motivation to build technical and consulting skills with guidance from experienced practitioners.

Additional Preferred Experience

Air quality permitting support experience and exposure to emissions modeling or regulatory strategy development.
Familiarity with CEQA and California environmental permitting requirements.
Exposure to environmental engineering, including stormwater management and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) planning.
Experience supporting proposals, cost estimates or project planning.
Experience or demonstrated interest in emerging energy sectors, including hydrogen, carbon capture and management, renewable power and biofuels.

Compensation

For California applicants

Salary Range: $85,398 - $113,821; based upon experience
Benefits: eligible for PTO, 401k, medical, vision, dental, etc.

Los Angeles

We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles' Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

Application of the pay band: Variation in salary is determined by factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.

Benefits

Feel the energy at Worley with access to a range of benefits including paid time off, holiday pay (usually 8 per year in the US), and eligibility to participate in the medical, life, dental, and vision insurance plans, as well as 401K plan.

Apply today

Bring your environmental permitting experience, curiosity and collaborative approach to a role where you can contribute to meaningful projects while continuing to develop as a trusted environmental professional.

You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners, work across multidisciplinary teams, gain exposure to clients and regulators, and broaden your experience across established and emerging energy markets. As your expertise develops, you will have opportunities to take on greater technical, project delivery and client responsibilities.

About Us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today’s needs and transition to more sustainable solutions. Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.

Moving forward together

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We’re building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it. We’re reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today’s low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.

jobs.description:
Overview

ABOUT THE POSITION

Senior Water Resources Engineer – Lead Cutting-Edge Hydraulics & Resiliency Projects Across New England

VHB’s Water Resources group is rapidly expanding across New England, and we’re seeking a senior-level Water Resources Engineer with deep hydraulics and hydrology expertise to help lead our high-performing team. As climate change happens it drives more frequent and intense weather/storm events, our clients are turning to VHB to deliver technically rigorous, resilient, and future-ready water resources solutions—and you can be at the center of that work.

Ideally based in the Greater Boston area, we would consider someone based in any of our New England offices. In this highly visible role, you’ll be a trusted technical leader and strategic advisor to public and private clients, developing innovative and cost-effective solutions to complex riverine and coastal flooding, ecological restoration, and water resources challenges. You’ll apply advanced H&H analysis and modeling on projects that span site to watershed scale, working alongside an integrated network of experienced water resources professionals across the region.

Responsibilities

Leading multi-disciplinary projects with hydrologic, hydraulic, and resiliency focus including interaction with staff and clients
Conducting hydrologic, hydraulic and scour studies for riverine and coastal environments using current modeling software including HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, HydroCAD, HY-8, EPA SWMM, SRH-2D/SMS, CHAMP, and others
Using analysis to identify and design flood, scour and resiliency improvements including both hardened features and nature based solutions and living shorelines
Performing FEMA “no-rise” analyses and assisting clients with FEMA map revisions
Developing technical reports, design plans, construction documents, and specifications for water resources related projects
Leading the construction administration for water resource projects
Work with VHB’s integrated team to evaluate permit requirements and support the development of permit applications
Attend and present at meetings with clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders
Lead the development of project proposals, scopes of work and fee estimates
Mentoring and expanding the technical resources of our staff

Skills And Abilities

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills
Team-oriented with strong capability to motivate others
Must demonstrate superior ability in collaborative problem solving with stakeholders, clients, and teammates
Advanced understanding of hydrologic and hydraulic modeling programs, and the ability to select an apply to appropriate approach to solve our client’s problem
Experience and interest in staff development
Understanding of local, state, and federal permitting

Qualifications

A minimum of 11+ years experience in related water resource engineering and analysis required
BS in Civil/Environmental Engineering (a master’s degree may be substituted for 2 years of experience)
PE license
This high priority role offers an exclusive sign-on bonus*

The full-time annual base salary range for this position is $145,000 to $200,000. The base salary offered will be determined based on job-related factors, including geographic location, internal equity, experience, credentials, skills, education, work schedule, and other factors permitted by law. The posted salary range reflects base pay only. Additional compensation and benefits available to eligible employees are outlined in our Total Rewards Program.

Annual base salary is one component of VHB’s Total Rewards package. In addition to base pay, eligible employees may receive annual incentive compensation bonuses, spot bonuses, and merit-based salary increases, providing opportunities to increase earnings beyond base pay. VHB also offers a differentiating work experience , including a comprehensive benefits package that includes eligibility to participate in the VHB 401(k) plan, medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, wellness programs, tuition reimbursement, and recognition programs.

Details on VHB’s benefits package can be found here: Benefits Checklist

VHB, was honored for excellence in strategy, execution, corporate culture, and governance/financial performance. Sponsored by Deloitte Private and The Wall Street Journal

Building What’s Next, Together.

Our people make the difference. We foster a technology-empowered, people‑driven, future‑ready culture where agility, innovation, and collaboration shape how we work every day.

Meaningful work on complex projects with real community impact
A collaborative, inclusive culture that values curiosity and shared success
Support to grow your skills and lead through change
Learning and development supported by evolving tools and technologies, including AI
Best-in-class benefits and a flexible, hybrid work environment

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist - BLUvera
jobs.description:
Summary

BLUvera, Mortenson’s vertically integrated manufacturing and fabrication affiliate, is currently seeking a Senior Environmental Specialist to develop and run the environmental compliance program for our mid-sized, fast-growing manufacturing and prefabrication business. This role will assess current compliance gaps, resolve issues, and develop standard processes and procedures for environmental permitting, waste management, inspections, and facility start-up and close-out as our operations grow and change.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and lead the environmental compliance program for a fast-growing manufacturing business
Conduct environmental compliance gap analyses across facilities and drive identified issues through to resolution
Establish standard processes and procedures to ensure proper environmental permitting, waste management, inspections, and issue resolution
Obtain, maintain, and ensure compliance with environmental permits, with a primary focus on waste, air, and wastewater
Manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste programs in compliance with RCRA requirements
Prepare and submit required regulatory reports, including SARA Title III / Tier II reporting
Conduct facility environmental inspections and support regulatory agency inspections
Lead environmental close-out activities as the business moves out of facilities, including permit closures, waste removal, and required documentation
Support environmental due diligence for property acquisitions and leases
Develop and lead environmental training programs
Maintain operational knowledge of environmental issues in manufacturing, and other applicable standards, regulations, laws, and procedures
Communicate with various third parties including regulatory representatives, environmental consultants, waste vendors, and landlords

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, environmental management, environmental science, or related field of study
Minimum of six years of related experience
Demonstrated environmental compliance experience and expertise in a manufacturing environment
Strong working knowledge of RCRA requirements and compliance
Experience with SARA Title III / Tier II reporting
Experience with environmental permitting and inspections, particularly for waste, air, and wastewater
Proven ability to build and run an environmental program in a growing organization, including gap analysis, issue resolution, and developing standard processes and procedures
Deep understanding of Federal, State, Provincial and local laws, policies, and procedures
Strong organization and self-direction skills with the ability to collaborate in a team atmosphere
Ability to communicate with consultants and governmental agencies
Current driver’s license
Ability to travel up to 25%
Preferred: Experience with environmental due diligence for property acquisition and leasing

A Few Benefits Offered Include

(for Non-Craft & Non-Union Craft working 25+ hours / week)

Medical and prescription drug plans that includes no additional cost vision coverage
Dental plan
401k retirement plan with a generous Mortenson match
Paid time off, holidays, and other paid leaves
Employer paid Life, AD&D, and disability insurance
No-Cost mental health tool and concierge with extensive work-life resources
Tuition reimbursement
Adoption Assistance
Gym Membership Discount Program

The base pay range for this role is $98,800 - $133,300. (Actual range is higher for the following office locations: Denver, CO and Chicago, IL – 5%, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR – 10%, Washington, D.C. – 12.5%).

Base pay is positioned within the range based on several factors including an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience, with consideration given to internal equity. This position is eligible for Mortenson’s incentive plan.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Environmental Health Science - RISE EARTH
jobs.description:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through the internal application process.

Job Category:

Faculty

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Assistant Professor

Job Summary:

The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Department of Population Health Sciences at the University of Wisconsin–Madison invite outstanding environmental health scientists to apply for a joint appointment, tenure-track position for an Assistant or Associate Professor in environmental health as part of the Wisconsin RISE-EARTH (Environment: Adaptation, Resilience, Technology, and Humanity) initiative. We seek scholars who demonstrate high potential for developing an extramurally funded epidemiology research program at UW-Madison. While any candidates with advanced (PhD or MD and Master combination) training in environmental health will be considered, highly competitive candidates will have training and scholarship in one or more of the following areas of epidemiology: air pollution epidemiology, human health effects of contaminants in drinking water, biomarker and/or other environmental exposure and risk assessment, and measurement and analysis of lifetime environmental exposures on human health (exposome).

This position is part of the Wisconsin Research, Innovation and Scholarly Excellence (RISE) Initiative. Through accelerated and strategic faculty hiring, research infrastructure enhancement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and increased student and educational opportunities, RISE addresses complex societal challenges of importance to the state, nation and world. Building on UW–Madison’s strengths, RISE expands the University’s successful track record of connecting with communities and industry on collaborative solutions.

Over the next three academic years, UW–Madison will substantially increase current hiring levels, bringing 150 new RISE faculty to campus. Candidates hired through RISE will join a community of scholars working across disciplines, schools and colleges on research, teaching and outreach endeavors. The community will engage regularly in venues such as seminar series and colloquia to share ongoing projects and identify opportunities to work together. The University will support the community, facilitating access to research infrastructure, and funding to support broad and rich collaboration.

Further information regarding RISE can be found at: https://rise.wisc.edu/.

Environmental public health involves interdisciplinary collaboration researching determinants of disease along causal pathways of exposure through to health outcomes. This hire, therefore, will be joint between the Nelson Institute and the Department of Population Health Sciences.

Research areas within environmental health may include, but not be limited to human health effects of: exposure to contaminants in air, water, soil, or food, climate change, noise, and environmental health effects of emerging technologies. We welcome applications from scholars employing observational or experiment studies, longitudinal or cross-sectional designs, and/or mathematical modeling of environmental health risk.

In addition to a joint appointment in the Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies (75%) and the Department of Population Health Sciences (25%), affiliations with other departments, centers, and institutes across campus are possible. This faculty appointment will be on an annual (12-month) pay basis. In addition, a generous start-up package including flexible research funds will be available for qualified candidates.

The Nelson Institute is a freestanding division of the university, serving more than one thousand undergraduate and graduate students, and home two dozen faculty from across the physical, biological, and social sciences and the humanities. It also houses four interdisciplinary research centers that serve as cross-campus laboratories and incubators for solutions to the world’s most critical environmental challenges. These include: the Center for Climatic Research, the Center for Culture, History and Environment, the Center for Sustainability and the Global Environment (SAGE) that includes an environmental health focus, and the Center for Ecology and the Environment. The Institute has many partnerships in education, research and community service that promote a more environmentally, economically and socially sustainable world. The Institute offers an undergraduate major and certificates in environmental studies, and sustainability. Graduate students pursue MS and PhD degrees in environmental conservation, environmental observation and informatics, environment and resources, or water resources management; and certificates in energy analysis and policy or culture, history, and environment. The institute also stewards the Office of Sustainability Research and Education for the UW-Madison campus.

Population Health Sciences is an interdisciplinary department with the goal of understanding, preserving, and improving the health of populations and individuals. The candidate selected for this role will contribute to the advancement of this mission through research, teaching, and service, and interact with a collaborative community of scholars throughout SMPH and across campus. The ideal candidate will have experience working within interdisciplinary teams. The successful applicant will develop and lead an extramurally funded research program in environmental epidemiology, teach courses or equivalent research direction during the academic year, and participate in administrative and committee work to support the mission of the School of Medicine and Public Health and the Nelson Institute. An essential part of these duties will be working in a collegial relationship with other faculty members.

Madison is the state's capitol city and is well known for offering a small town feel in a medium sized city. It is a great place to raise a family and offers an ideal combination of natural beauty, stimulating cultural events, outstanding schools and outdoor recreation.

Key Job Responsibilities:

10% Service:

Participate in faculty governance and service to the department, school, university, and profession, as appropriate.

30% Teaching:

Teach 9 credits (or equivalent) annually of courses or credited research direction in environmental health and PHS/Environmental epidemiology.. Advise and mentor graduate students in the Nelson Institute, PHS Population Health and Epidemiology programs and other relevant degree programs at UW-Madison.

The successful applicant will participate in interdisciplinary and collaborative efforts with other departments, schools and colleges.

The successful applicant will participate in administrative and committee work to support the clinical and scholarly missions of the Nelson Institute and School of Medicine and Public Health. An essential part of these duties will be working in a collegial relationship with other faculty members. Especially desirable is an ability to engage and interact with interdisciplinary communities and an enthusiasm for team-building within and beyond the health sciences to include physical systems sciences, social sciences and the humanities.

The successful candidate, depending on their background, will teach graduate and undergraduate students, medical students, residents, and fellows.

60% Research:

Develop and maintain an independent program of research in environmental epidemiology. Research programs may include but are not limited to innovative study of air pollution epidemiology, human health effects of contaminants in drinking water, biomarker and other environmental exposure assessment, health risks from climate change and energy policy, and exposome measurement and analysis.

Department:

The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Department of Population Health Sciences

Compensation:

Negotiable – 12-month / full-time (100%) / ongoing / renewable Actual pay will depend on experience and qualifications.
This position offers a comprehensive benefits package, including generous sick leave, competitively priced health/dental/vision/life insurance, tax-advantaged savings accounts, and participation in the nationally recognized Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS) pension fund. For a summary of benefits, please see https://www.wisconsin.edu/ohrwd/benefits/download/fasl.pdf.

Required Qualifications:

Candidates should demonstrate evidence of creativity and excellence in teaching and scholarly research as well as the ability to make valuable contributions to the department, college, and RISE initiative. Application materials for this tenure-track position in environment epidemiology should communicate capacity to conduct cutting-edge research, teach/mentor undergraduates and graduate students, and participate in department and university service. In addition, the successful candidate will demonstrate fostering or the ability to foster a teaching, learning, mentoring, departmental, and research environment where all can thrive.

Hiring rank will be commensurate with years of relevant experience. To be hired at the associate professor level, candidates must possess experience and scholarly credentials that meet the tenure standards of the UW-Madison Divisional Committee and of the Nelson Institute.

All requirements must be met by the position start date.

Preferred Qualifications:

Education:

Terminal Degree (PhD, MD or DrPH) is required by the start date of the position.

How to Apply:

Apply online at "Jobs at UW" (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under Job Requisition JR10016349. Applications must be received through UW- Madison's online application system. Applications submitted outside of this system will not be considered. Click the "Apply Now" button to start the application process. Applicants should submit the following items:

a letter of application,
curriculum vitae,
a research statement

You will be asked to provide the names and contact information of three (3) references who are well-respected authorities in the field. For those who advance in the process, references will be contacted to provide letters of recommendation. Candidates will be notified prior to contacting references.

To ensure consideration, complete applications must be received by 11:59pm (CST) on December 7, 2026.
Applications will be accepted until position is filled. Please note that applicants will be evaluated based upon submitted application materials and therefore should speak to and include evidence of their qualifications.

Please note that successful applicants are responsible for ensuring their eligibility to work in the United States (i.e. a citizen or national of the United States, a lawful permanent resident, a foreign national authorized to work in the United States without need of employer sponsorship) on or before the effective date of appointment. UW-Madison is not an E-Verify employer, and therefore, is not eligible to employ F-1 STEM OPT Extension participants.

Contact Information:

Lili Gagliano, asu.hr@ohr.wisc.edu

Institutional Statement on Diversity:

Diversity is a source of strength, creativity, and innovation for UW-Madison. We value the contributions of each person and respect the profound ways their identity, culture, background, experience, status, abilities, and opinion enrich the university community. We commit ourselves to the pursuit of excellence in teaching, research, outreach, and diversity as inextricably linked goals.

The University of Wisconsin-Madison fulfills its public mission by creating a welcoming and inclusive community for people from every background - people who as students, faculty, and staff serve Wisconsin and the world.

Job Summary

Environmental Specialist is responsible for developing, communicating, and implementing waste related environmental programs, evaluating environmental data, ensuring regulatory compliance for various company business units and facilities, in a safe, compliant, and cost-effective manner. This role involves ensuring proper characterization and disposal of various environmental media, working with various waste vendors, Environmental regulators (State and Federal), transporters, TSDFs, conducting site visits and providing on-site guidance for on-going projects, and providing recommendations to minimize environmental risks and promote responsible environmental stewardship.

Work Responsibilites

May involve travel to facilities, project sites, or regulatory meetings.
Occasional work in construction, utility, or environmental remediation settings.
Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) may be required during field inspections.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, biology, chemistry, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance or environmental management experience.
Knowledge of environmental regulations such as:
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)
Toxic Substance Control Act (TSCA)
Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act (EPCRA)
Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)
Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA)
Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act
OSHA environmental requirements
Department of Transportation (DOT)

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Experience working with regulatory agencies and compliance programs.

Waste Management and Compliance

Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Identify, classify, and manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste.
Coordinate waste disposal activities with approved vendors and treatment facilities.

Maintain waste profiles, manifests, and tracking records.
Monitor waste generation trends and identify opportunities for reduction.
Ensure accurate labeling, storage, and transportation of waste materials.

Operational Support

Coordinate with operations, maintenance, and other site personnel.
Ensure waste handling equipment is properly maintained and used safely.
Conduct environmental inspections and audits.

Train employees in waste handling procedures and environmental requirements.
Communicate regulatory changes and best practices.
Develop standard operating procedures (SOPs) for waste management activities.

Environmental compliance management
Waste characterization and classification
Regulatory reporting
Hazardous material handling
Data analysis and recordkeeping
Vendor management
Auditing and inspections
Problem solving and continuous improvement

About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview

Vantage is seeking a Director of Environmental Compliance, North America
to lead environmental compliance programs across a growing portfolio of mission-critical data center campuses. This role serves as the senior environmental compliance leader for the region and is responsible for ensuring an audit-ready compliance posture, managing environmental risk, and maintaining regulatory compliance across both active construction projects and live operating facilities.

The Director will provide strategic leadership for environmental programs, air quality compliance, spill prevention, stormwater management, waste management, environmental audits, regulatory engagement, and environmental management systems. This position partners closely with Operations, Construction, Legal, and the broader EHS team to ensure environmental requirements are effectively integrated into business operations and growth initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance & Regulatory Leadership

Lead environmental compliance programs across North America.
Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, provincial, and local environmental regulations.
Oversee implementation of environmental permits, regulatory reporting, inspections, audits, and agency interactions.
Maintain environmental compliance systems, obligation registers, and compliance calendars.
Monitor emerging regulatory developments and assess business impacts.

Environmental Risk Management

Identify, assess, and manage environmental risks across construction and operational campuses.
Integrate environmental requirements into project development, design reviews, commissioning, and operations.
Partner with business leaders to proactively address environmental compliance risks and liabilities.

Air, Water & Waste Compliance

Oversee compliance programs related to:
Air permits and emissions reporting; emergency generators and obligations regarding stationary combustion sources

Stormwater and wastewater compliance
Hazardous waste

Environmental Audits & Assurance

Track corrective actions and verify closure effectiveness.
Prepare sites for customer, internal, and regulatory inspections.
Provide executive reporting on environmental compliance performance and emerging risks.

Environmental Incident Response

Manage investigations, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and regulatory notifications.
Support emergency preparedness and environmental response exercises.

Experience managing air permits, SPCC programs, stormwater compliance, waste management, and regulatory reporting.

Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Experience building and leading teams of environmental professionals.

jobs.description:
Job Title:
Health, Safety & Environmental Specialist

Job Description:

Trystar is a leader in portable and permanent power distribution solutions. The HSE Specialist is responsible for ensuring all safety and environmental programs, procedures, training, work practices and controls are effectively implemented at our Houston, TX facilities. This position is accountable for identifying applicable EHS regulations and risks while interacting with Operations, Quality, Planning, Legal, and Engineering to support and maintain systems in order to ensure compliance and conformance to all Trystar HSE Policies, Programs, Work Instructions, and Management Systems. This role will report to Trystar HSE Manager.

We are looking for people who believe in our guiding principles and values of:

Safety – We believe everyone should leave Trystar facilities in the same or better condition than when they arrived.
Integrity – We’re honest, transparent, and committed to doing what’s right.
Customer focus – We have relentless focus on our customers and their success.
Right with speed – We use good judgement, make thoughtful decisions quickly, and execute them with purpose and intensity.
Play for each other – We’re a team. We show up for each other and we know that through teamwork we achieve greatness.
Champion change – We know adaptation and improvement are requirements to survive and to thrive.
Enjoy the journey – We create an environment where our team feels appreciated and has fun along the way.

In this role you will get to:

Facilitate EHS program objectives by providing clear and continuous direction to site.
Utilize existing proactive safety tools & deploy improvements as needed.
Train and coach operations staff on accident prevention and reduction activities & ensure safety is at the forefront of all factory discussions.
Provide expertise on safety risk identification, assessment and management processes at site level.
Be the site EHS expert and preferred point of contact for safety and environmental inquiries.
Complete site compliance activities to ensure company and regulatory requirements are met in relation to safety, health, waste management, water discharge, air observation as well as assisting in permit obligations.
Monitor EHS federal, state, and local regulatory requirements and risk initiatives; analyze potential impacts on system operations; provide operations and sr. leadership with information as appropriate.
Identify & facilitate health and safety training for Company staff, subcontractors, and any parties required to participate to ensure achievement of exceptional health & safety performance including developing training content and delivering course information through in-house or external resources.
Drive coordination and engagement of plant & support personnel in the identification, development, and implementation of HSE goals which will positively impact and add value to the organization.
Maintain HSE documents, permit administration utilizing appropriate retention rules.
Provide leadership to site emergency response teams and safety committee teams.
Partner with HR for orientation training and to manage workers compensation cases.
Maintain continued presence on floor as an observer, leader, trainer, and main point of contact for HSE assistance.
Support incident reporting process and participate in incident investigation and root cause analysis and ensure deficiencies are corrected in a timely manner and to acceptable measures.
Provide manufacturing & engineering technical input into process hazard studies and capital projects ensuring safety is at the forefront of processes & projects. Provide oversight to subcontractors and project team members to ensure that project activities are completed according to applicable accident prevention plans.
Acts as site point of contact for all safety related matters and provides day-to-day advice & guidance on process safety issues at the site.
Conduct regular inspections and audits to assess health and safety plan adherence as well as identify potential loss and risk.
Interface effectively with manufacturing supervisors and management team, escalating issues appropriately and making recommendations regarding policy & procedure.
Assist in the development of the HSE budget for the site.
Attend site management and department meetings on regular basis and upon request.
Ensure safety program compliance to include but not limited to:
LOTO, Electrical, Confined Space, PPE, PIT, Hearing Conservation, Respiratory Protection

Support health program compliance to include but not limited to:
Industrial Hygiene plan development for personal exposure monitoring

Drive environmental program compliance to include but not limited to:
Air Permitting, Regulatory Reporting, Waste Management, Wastewater, Storm Water

Job Requirements:

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Health, Safety, Environmental or related field
Three years of progressive work experience in a position directly related to health and safety within a manufacturing environment
Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish required, with the ability to communicate effectively in both written and verbal settings.
Strong ability to communicate in written and oral formats with diplomacy and tact
Competent in using Microsoft Office products, email systems, and Windows
Ability to communicate in Spanish as a second language preferred
Ability to travel up to 25% to visit other sites and support with safety audits and initiatives

Additional Qualifications

Demonstrated success in teaching others health and safety concepts and requirements
ASP or GSP preferred
Successful leadership in manufacturing facilities & work project teams in support of health & safety endeavors
An aptitude for exercising independent thinking and reasoning
Previous success in working effectively in a cross functional environment
Skilled in leading others without formal reporting authority
Flexibility to work extended, earlier or later hours periodically to support projects and shift schedules

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Geologist
jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

Arcadis is seeking an entry-level
Geologist/Environmental Scientist to join our team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA. While this position requires both field and office work, the candidate should expect to spend 50% to 75% of their time in the field.

You will have the opportunity to join a dedicated team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA that prioritizes mentorship and your professional growth. The team is committed to supporting your success and providing guidance as you navigate your role.

We are currently considering candidates available for an immediate start and those seeking a Summer 2027 start date.

As part of our Resilience Environment team, you’ll help improve quality of life.

Role accountabilities:

As part of this role, you will be responsible for assisting Project Managers (PMs) and Task Managers (TMs) in planning and executing environmental site characterization, investigation, and remediation tasks.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. It is essential to conduct fieldwork with a focus on health and safety.

Your core duties will include:

Prepare subcontracts and oversee the work of subcontractors.
Writing and preparing technical reports, work plans, letters, and memoranda
Office work may include task coordination, data compilation and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file reviews, proposal writing, project strategy development, schedule and budget management, and establishment of subcontracts.
Conduct field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work. Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable. A valid driver's license is required for the role.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Hydrogeology, or closely related field (i.e., environmental science, physical science)

Preferred Qualifications

Master of Science degree in Geology or closely related field
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training 

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $63,480- $95,220. Actual salaries will vary and are based on several factors, such as experience, education, budget, internal equity, project and location.

Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Environmental Data Manager
to join our team in Oakland, Walnut Creek, Davis, or Sacramento, California
. In this role, you will support the development and management of environmental data systems, workflows, and quality processes for multidisciplinary projects involving environmental assessment, groundwater remediation, water resources, geotechnical construction, and related services. You will combine environmental chemistry expertise with strong database, automation, and client-service skills to deliver accurate, accessible, and decision-ready information.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Design, develop, and manage project-specific relational database applications using enterprise platforms such as Microsoft SQL Server and EQuIS.
Create documented workflows and metadata that automate the integration of data from multiple sources and deliver it to maps, reports, dashboards, and other tools.
Manage environmental datasets across the full data lifecycle, from planning and collection through analysis and final reporting.
Establish and perform QA/QC for environmental data, systems, and related processes.
Compile, verify, analyze, and report large, complex, and diverse datasets.
Coordinate with laboratories, consultants, agencies, and other internal and external data providers to support accurate, timely data collection and transfer.
Collect, transform, query, and analyze environmental analytical, geologic, geotechnical, and geospatial data.
Interact with internal and external clients to deliver database management and data-visualization solutions for environmental, engineering, and geoscience projects.
Drive personal , company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

You will collaborate with experienced professionals across disciplines while contributing your own technical expertise and perspective. Geosyntec supports continuous learning, encourages employees to deepen their interests and skills, and recognizes advancement through performance, initiative, and impact.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor's degree in environmental science, chemistry, geography, computer science, engineering, or geology. (required)
Advanced degree in environmental science, chemistry, geography, computer science, engineering, or geology. (preferred)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

Demonstrated experience managing databases and developing ETL processes. ( required)
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Access, including complex formulas and effective data visualization. (required)
Ability to write complex SQL queries and automate routine processes. (required)
Experience automating processes with scripting languages such as Python or R. (required)
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities. (required)
Exceptional attention to detail across quantitative work products and written communications. (required)
Proficiency with EarthSoft’s EQuIS environmental data management platform. (preferred)
Direct experience managing environmental, geologic, and geotechnical data collection. (preferred)
Knowledge of laboratory analytical data verification and validation processes. (preferred)
Experience submitting data to and retrieving data from agency and government databases, including California Water Boards GeoTracker, CIWQS, NIRIS, ERPIMS, and CEDEN. (preferred)
Valid U.S. driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

jobs.title: Chemical Regulatory Compliance Specialist 2
jobs.description:
L-H Battery Company, Inc., located in Jeffersonville, Ohio, is a Joint venture of LG Energy Solution and Honda to manufacture large lithium-ion polymer batteries. Products from L-H Battery power a variety of innovative energy storage applications.

Established in 2023, L-H Battery is passionate about developing and maintaining a culture where our associates and customers understand their value and worth. We are making a positive impact, and we want you to be a part of it!

Summary

Responsible for the day-to-day administration and oversight of the site's Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) compliance program. The role evaluates chemicals, mixtures, articles, raw materials, components, and process changes for applicable TSCA requirements before import, purchase, manufacture, processing, use, distribution, or disposition. The Specialist maintains defensible compliance records, coordinates cross-functional controls, monitors regulatory changes, supports reporting and notifications, and helps ensure that regulated substances and articles are managed in accordance with applicable federal requirements and company procedures.

Key Responsibilities

Administer the site's TSCA compliance program and maintain procedures, work instructions, decision records, and compliance calendars for applicable TSCA obligations.
Review new chemicals, mixtures, raw materials, battery materials, components, articles, and process changes before procurement, import, manufacture, processing, use, distribution, recycling, transfer, or disposal.
Confirm chemical identities and regulatory status using supplier documentation, Safety Data Sheets, Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) numbers, composition data, and applicable EPA resources; document inventory, exemption, exclusion, and article determinations.
Evaluate whether planned activities may require review under TSCA Section 5, including premanufacture, significant new use, low-volume, research-and-development, polymer, or other applicable new-chemical requirements.
Track site-specific manufacture and import volumes and coordinate data collection, applicability reviews, quality checks, and submissions for Chemical Data Reporting and other applicable TSCA reporting obligations.
