jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe transportation is more than movement, it’s the foundation of connected, thriving communities. As part of HDR’s Transportation Business Group, you’ll help shape the systems that move people and goods safely, efficiently, and sustainably. From designing resilient highways and iconic bridges to advancing transit, passenger and freight rail, aviation, federal transportation ports and marine infrastructure, your work will directly support economic vitality, public safety, sustainable and resilient communities and quality of life. We bring together planners, engineers, architects, construction management staff, environmental, strategic communications, economists, management consultants and specialists across disciplines to solve complex mobility challenges with innovation, technical excellence, and a deep understanding of community needs. Whether you're modernizing aging infrastructure or pioneering next-generation transportation solutions, your contributions will help define the future of mobility. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to lead progress, drive meaningful impact, and leave a legacy of smarter, more connected transportation networks. We are all employee-owners at HDR, which is the foundation of our collaborative culture that connects employees around the world.

HDR is looking for an Environmental Sciences and Planning Lead to join our Transportation Business Group in North Carolina. Working internally as part of our Professional Services program, the Environmental Sciences and Planning Lead will be expected to provide leadership and management support for staff development, quality technical delivery, and coordinated functions within the local area Environmental Sciences and Planning (ES&P) Business Class. This is a cross-sector position and will report to the North Carolina Transportation Business Group but will further collaborate with HDR’s Water, Resources, and Federal groups for overall resource allocation, key hires, quality control, and technical excellence. They will interact and lead HDR environmental sciences and planning staff NEPA/SEPA practitioners and other multi-disciplinary staff. They will work closely with HDR leadership to drive program development in North Carolina focusing on transportation resource clients/projects. They should possess a balanced portfolio of skills to assist with business development which requires networking and developing leads, establishing/managing client relationships, and strategic thinking for both our clients and internal programs.

In the role of Environmental Sciences and Planning Lead, we'll count on you to:

Take responsibility for operations of production including staff development, profitability, morale, quality control and marketing support.
Function as a Project Manager and take responsibility for production on projects in addition to management responsibilities.
Have a focus on client management and development, serving as a client manager and project manager for future assignments and pursuits with key clients in the area.
Take administrative responsibility for section staff and technical service functions, and lead and coordinate services with other sections.
Be involved in marketing planning, proposals and interviews.
Be directly involved with clients in marketing, project production and related issues.
See that all work is planned, organized, controlled and evaluated through proactive project management system
Implement, monitor and support company policy.
Select, train, develop and manage technical personnel.
Manage and develop multidiscipline teams.
Work cooperatively with marketing staff in local and national marketing and production efforts.
Plan and direct planning and environmental projects.
Prepare, plan and analyze/review technical studies, permit applications, NEPA documents, and similar reports/documents.
Direct work of others in completion of required studies, documents and reports.
Demonstrate extensive public participation, agency coordination, planning and programming experience.
Perform other duties as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

15 years of experience
Master’s degree in environmental science, planning, or related
Experience writing proposals, developing scopes of work, budgets, and schedules for complex environmental projects with multidisciplinary teams and multi-agency efforts, local candidates are preferred
NEPA experience including EIS, EA, and CE, MCDCs, or equivalents
Regulatory permitting experience with 404/401/CAMA/Buffers

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
A minimum of 10 years experience
Professional registration, license or certification may be required based on role
Strong communication and listening skills
Ability to handle multiple assignments
Good leadership and organizational skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

General Description And Classification Standards

Performs supervisory assignments associated with operating the water/wastewater treatment plant and to ensure a continuous, adequate supply of potable drinking water meeting federal/state regulations for the citizens of Atlanta. Supervises; water analysis and treatment; mixing chemicals; laboratory testing; operating various pumps and valves; repairing and maintaining machinery and equipment; maintaining records, instructing and disciplining assigned staff. This is a team lead or "foreman" level position with a formally designated team of skilled employees, either in one or multiple skilled specialties. Lead assignments made on a job-by-job basis would be more appropriately at the Senior level. Supervision Received Direction received is very general and focuses on end results and is typically collaborative in nature. Makes decisions on technical issues, diagnoses, or procedures in collaboration with supervisors or managers.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

These are typical responsibilities for this position and should not be construed as exclusive or all inclusive. May perform other duties as assigned. Generates work orders in maintenance management system; orders chemicals and supplies. Coordinates with contractors on plant upgrades and equipment repairs and installations. Responsible for maintaining the facility in a condition that meets state and federal permit requirements. Reviews the work of Operators for accuracy/completion and to ensure compliance with local, state and federal regulations. Communicates with employees to ensure proper plant operation of the Standard Operating Procedures. Prepares and maintaining reports, logs, and records on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis. Controls treatment plant processes, chemical dosages, and equipment used to purify, treat and clarify water for human consumption and for industrial and commercial use. Assists in performing a variety of laboratory tests to determine the chemical composition of water and to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations for turbidity, chlorine, fluoride, pH, iron and manganese; makes adjustments to chemical dosages as necessary. Records plant operation data from observations, instrumentation and laboratory tests; records test results for reporting to state agency as appropriate. Receives and/or prepares letters, reports, correspondence, forms and other documentation; reviews, processes, and/or forwards as appropriate; maintains files and logs; performs other clerical duties.

Decision Making

Selects from multiple procedures and methods to accomplish tasks. Applies organizational policies. Leadership Provided Has formal supervisory authority over work group (typically at least 4-5 employees) to include discipline, performance management, scheduling, training, etc.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Knowledge of the operation, methods and procedures of a wastewater treatment plant; knowledge of the machinery used for wastewater treatment and pumping stations; knowledge of mechanical equipment; knowledge of basic machinery preventive maintenance and repair; knowledge of State and Federal rules governing wastewater discharges and worker's safety; knowledge of laboratory procedures and terminology; knowledge of Chemistry terminology; knowledge of microorganisms; knowledge of Back Flow Prevention. Ability to use independent judgment and discretion in managing subordinates including the handling of emergency situations, determining and deciding upon procedures to be implemented, setting priorities, maintaining standards, and resolving problems; ability to comprehend, interpret, and apply regulations, procedures, and related information; ability to handle required mathematical calculations; ability to treat water in a safe, effective manner; ability to work outdoors in any kind of weather; ability to read and understand design drawings and plans; ability to operate a vehicle; ability to diagnose and correct equipment malfunctions.

jobs.title: Project Environmental Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Overview

APTIM is seeking a Project Environmental Data Analyst
that will work exclusively on a Key Client National Account to manage client and vendor data sets presented in various formats and turn them into reliable datasets, project databases, and useful Power BI Dashboards. The Environmental Data Analyst will work with project managers and technical specialists to understand reporting needs, recommend meaningful metrics and trend analyses, evaluate data workflows, and independently build and maintain tools from initial requirements through ongoing use. The successful candidate will have advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI skills, sound analytical judgment, and the ability to deliver accurate, understandable information that supports client reporting and project decisions. Environmental data and AI experience are valued but are not required.

Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities

Partner with project managers and technical specialists to define reporting objectives, identify relevant metrics and trends, and translate project questions into practical data tools and dashboards.
Demonstrate expertise in data management, automation, and interactive business intelligence to transform multiple streams of raw data into automated reporting formats.
Combine, clean, standardize, and reconcile data across multiple Microsoft Excel workbooks, client data exports, vendor reports, and project databases; resolve inconsistent identifiers, formats, dates, units, duplicate records, and missing information.
Analyze datasets across sites, reporting periods, and data sources to identify trends, discrepancies, exceptions, and opportunities for improvement; explain findings and data limitations to the project team.
Design, build, and maintain Power BI reports and dashboards, including Power Query transformations, data models, relationships, DAX measures, filters, and clear visualizations tailored to client needs.
Evaluate existing data collection and reporting workflows; develop repeatable Excel and Power Query processes that reduce manual work and improve consistency and timeliness.
Build and maintain project databases and structured datasets, including tables, unique identifiers, relationships, validation rules, and data dictionaries that support reliable analysis and reporting.
Validate calculations and dashboard results against source records; document reconciliation checks, assumptions, and unresolved exceptions, and coordinate technical interpretation with environmental specialists.
Own ongoing tool maintenance, including data refreshes, troubleshooting, updates, and change testing to ensure accuracy.
Manage assigned data deliverables across the program’s datasets, estimate effort, meet agreed schedules, and communicate priorities and issues with limited day-to-day supervision.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, information systems, computer science, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in data analysis, data management, and support of tools used by project teams or clients.
Advanced Microsoft Excel proficiency, including complex formulas, lookup functions, PivotTables, data validation, Power Query, and combining and reconciling data across workbooks.
Demonstrated Power BI development experience including data preparation, relational modeling, DAX calculations, report design, publishing, and maintaining refresh processes in Power BI Service.
Ability to translate loosely defined reporting needs into working solutions, organize concurrent assignments, document methods, and explain results clearly to nontechnical users.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with environmental or EHS data, such as hazardous waste, stormwater, inspection findings, compliance tracking, or sustainability metrics; experience supporting consulting or client project delivery.
SQL querying skills and experience with database platforms or environmental data management systems.
Experience with Power Automate, VBA, Python, or similar tools to automate data preparation and reporting.
Project management experience, including coordinating with cross-functional teams, managing schedules and deliverables, communicating risks and priorities, and supporting account managers to deliver successful client project execution.
Experience applying AI tools to data extraction, reconciliation, analysis, or workflow automation, with validation of outputs and appropriate protection of client information.

Overview

ABOUT THE POSITION

VHB is seeking an Environmental Scientist / Project Manager to help support our growing Natural Sciences team. This hybrid field- and office-based role will support transportation, energy, land development, and infrastructure projects throughout Massachusetts and New England. This role could be based in either our Watertown or Worcester, MA offices locations.

Responsibilities

Manage environmental permitting, natural resource evaluation, and construction compliance tasks from scope development through delivery, including schedules, budgets, staffing, and client communication.
Lead and conduct wetland and watercourse delineations, wetland functional assessments, wildlife habitat evaluations, rare species surveys, and related field investigations.
Prepare and coordinate local, state, and federal environmental permit applications, supporting studies, alternatives analyses, technical reports, and agency responses.
Provide environmental compliance monitoring and reporting during construction, including erosion and sedimentation control oversight and permit-condition compliance.
Coordinate multidisciplinary internal teams, subconsultants, clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders; attend meetings and communicate project status, risks, and permitting strategies.
Review project deliverables for technical quality and mentor junior staff in field methods, permitting, reporting, and project-delivery practices.

Strong technical writing, quality-control, verbal communication, critical-thinking, and client-management skills.

Working knowledge of Massachusetts and federal environmental permitting, including the Wetlands Protection Act, Section 404/401, and the Massachusetts and federal Endangered Species Acts.

B.S. or M.S. in environmental science, natural resources, wetland science, soil science, ecological sciences, or a related field.

Proficient in ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and spatial database development

jobs.description:
Take Your Environmental Career to the Next Level

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step Into Your New Role

Kleinfelder is seeking an experienced Senior Air Quality Professional to join our team in the South Division!

The position is available in:

Charlotte, North Carolina
Raleigh, North Carolina
Atlanta, Georgia

The primary role of this position is to provide environmental and engineering technical support for various aspects of air quality compliance programs including:

preparation of emission inventories,
permit application development,
regulatory review,
compliance recordkeeping, and
greenhouse gas reporting

The applicant should have strong technical experience with air quality analyses and also have experience interacting with clients and regulatory agencies. The ideal candidate would also have experience mentoring junior level staff on technical work. This position will be expected to communicate with clients.

The applicant may also provide multi-media environmental compliance support to industrial, transportation, energy and other clients, to include: stormwater permitting, SPCC plan development, waste management support, compliance auditing, and industrial hygiene support. Additional activities may include site assessment and groundwater remediation support.

The candidate should have a working knowledge of Federal and various State air quality regulations.

Minimum Experience:

Emission calculations
Minor source permitting
Proficient with air emissions software such as E&P Tanks and GRI GlyCalc
Air quality regulations applicability determinations
Demonstrated expertise with environmental regulatory requirements in the southeastern United States
Project Management

Preferred Experience (beneficial but not required):

Air Dispersion modeling
Major source and Title V permitting
Demonstrated experience in the mining sector, with a focus on air compliance for mining operations
Project and/or Client management
Professional Engineering, Certified Hazardous Materials Manager or other professional certification

Professional Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, Environmental, or related
10+ years of related experience years of experience in Air Quality compliance
Proficient at communicating with clients and public
Proficient in Microsoft programs including Word and Excel
Strong experience with writing and communicating technical material
Some travel may be necessary

The successful candidate will be a part of Kleinfelder’s compliance hub of environmental experts that can support projects both regionally and throughout the United States.

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

 Kleinfelder and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, has been connecting great people to the best work since 1961. As a responsive, cross-disciplinary team of bright, curious, and innovative problem-solvers, we are dedicated to doing the right thing, every day, on every project from over 110 offices in the US, Canada, and Australia. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose – together, we deliver.

We support these efforts through reimbursements for continuing education as well as many of the expenses associated with trainings and certifications, and opportunities for career development through our internal Mentoring Program.

Introduction

We encourage you to consider an exciting career with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). If you are dedicated to protecting and preserving Maryland's air, water, land resources, and safeguarding the health of all its citizens, we invite you to apply and become a part of our team.

MDE is committed to a mission of protecting and restoring the environment for the health and well-being of all Marylanders, with a vision of healthy, vibrant, and sustainable communities and ecosystems throughout the state.

As part of our continuous efforts to optimize performance and drive success the Environmental Compliance Specialist I, is eligible for an annual promotion. The incumbent may advance to a higher grade within the classification series, based on satisfactory work performance.

Environmental Compliance Specialist II – Grade 15 ( $63,154.00-$99,603.00 )

Environmental Compliance Specialist III – Grade 16 ( $67,309.00-$106,155.00 )

Click here to learn more about MDE.

GRADE

STD0014

LOCATION OF POSITION

MDE - Water and Science Administration

Compliance Program, Central Division

1800 Washington Blvd.

Baltimore, MD 21230

Main Purpose of Job

The Environmental Compliance Specialist I is an entry-level position in the field of environmental regulatory compliance. The incumbents in these positions will represent MDE in a wide range of environmental program specialties, including water pollution control laws and regulations related to National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)/State Discharge Permits for municipal and industrial facilities, NPDES Pretreatment and industrial pretreatment program, Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) and sanitary sewer overflow (SSO) programs, Sediment and erosion control, Tidal and nontidal wetlands, Well and septic systems, and Waterway construction.

Employees in this position learn the process of environmental compliance through exposure to and interaction with other programs within WSA and MDE. At the trainee level, a strong emphasis is placed on compliance procedures and policies.

These are field positions, and the selected candidates will perform job duties in the following counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Charles, Harford, and St. Mary's.

Selected candidates will be required to report to the Baltimore Office at least once a week.
One selected candidate will be assigned to St. Mary’s County. This candidate will be required to report to St. Mary’s County up to four times a week and report to the Baltimore Office at least once a week.

The incumbent in this position will be required to drive a State vehicle.

Driver’s License
:
A valid driver’s license with no more than five points is required to operate a State vehicle.

Out-of-State Licenses
:
If you hold an out-of-state license, you must provide a certified copy of your driving record from the appropriate Motor Vehicle Administration at the time of appointment.

POSITION DUTIES

Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To The Following

Inspections and Investigations

Conduct inspections at permitted sites and investigate complaints.
Review and interpret permits/plan s , engineering drawings, schematics, Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs), Monthly Operating Reports, and historical records.
Perform on-site compliance consultations across wastewater, industrial, construction, agricultural, wetland, and dam safety sites.
Apply compliance assistance and pollution prevention strategies, including best management practices, self-inspections, environmental audits, and source reductions.
Inspect the installation, operation, and maintenance of pollution control devices, and examine business and public records to verify compliance.

Coordination and Communication

Represent the Compliance Program and the Water and Science Administration (WSA) with the regulated community, the public, and local, state, and federal agencies.
Interview permit holders, complainants, and subjects of complaints to gather facts and determine appropriate actions.
Correspond professionally with internal MDE departments, other state agencies, local regulatory partners, and NGOs.
Prepare complete and accurate reports in ETS, ensuring timely responses to all stakeholders.
Align operations with the WSA Climate Policy and MDE Environmental Justice (EJ) Policy.

Violations and Enforcement

Apply policies and criteria defining significant noncompliance.
Prepare digital enforcement and litigation packages for upper management review.

WORKING CONDITIONS

The working conditions for this position may involve exposure to uncomfortable or unpleasant surroundings.

Specialists visit an extensive range of sites, with consultations taking place in locations ranging from wetlands to sewage treatment plants and construction sites with loud, heavy equipment.
Most of the job involves working outdoors in all weather conditions, which may entail exposure to inclement weather, dust, potential chemicals, and pungent or unpleasant odors. Additionally, a significant amount of vehicle travel is required.
Hazardous conditions may exist at sites. Walking over rough surfaces and terrain on examining sediment traps, stormwater ponds and dikes around heavy equipment presents potentially dangerous conditions which could result in injury. Handling chemical testing agents and taking samples potentially exposes personnel to serious physical harm or impairment. Investigation of unauthorized facilities and/or sites can potentially cause exposure to known or unknown waste materials that can pose risk through physical, chemical, bacteriological, or radiological hazards for which training is provided. Also, natural biological hazards such as soil bacteria, allergens, ticks, rats, mosquitoes, snakes, can be encountered.
At some sites, water quality samples may be collected . This requires personnel to carry chemicals, equipment and tools, water samples, and files. Consultations conducted in the field require climbing over spoil piles, through rock lined ditches, crossing streams, etc.
Many consultations require the use of protective gear such as goggles and gloves to ensure that staff do not come into direct contact with harsh chemicals and toxic byproducts of industrial activity. Basic protective equipment will be provided. Incumbent is expected to provide suitable work clothes for dirty, dusty environments and all-weather conditions, including very hot and very cold weather.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants must satisfy the minimum qualifications to be considered for this position and move forward in the hiring process. Please read all requirements before applying.

Experience:
Four years of experience performing inspection or investigation work related to State, federal or local regulation, code or standard compliance.

Job Description

Only applicants who meet the Minimum Qualification Requirements and meet all selective requirements (listed below) will be placed on the

eligible list.

The Department of Natural Resources encourages all applicants to upload a current resume and cover letter to their online application.

Join the Iowa Department of Natural Resources Conservation and Recreation Division to coordinate sovereign lands construction permits and environmental reviews, utilizing spatial analysis and field surveys to support natural resource management across the state.

This position plays a central role in balancing natural resource protection with regulatory compliance by managing Environmental Review requests and Sovereign Land Construction Permit applications. In this role, you will evaluate proposed projects, coordinate closely with DNR Floodplains and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and serve as a primary liaison for applicants, consulting engineers, and the public through meetings, formal correspondence, and community hearings. Alongside permitting oversight, you will contribute directly to environmental policy development by researching complex issues, and presenting recommendations to agency leadership.

In the field and behind the scenes, you will assist biological investigations that drive data management for state conservation efforts. You will conduct ecological, botanical, and zoological field surveys, and analyze species and habitat data. Additionally, you will leverage GIS, database tools, and web applications to maintain and enhance the Iowa Natural Areas Inventory (INAI), translating vital plant and wildlife records into spatial analyses, maps, and reporting tools that inform conservation decisions across the division.

Essential Functions

Process incoming Environmental Review (ER) requests and Sovereign Land Construction Permit applications in compliance with applicable state, federal, and local standards and align permit actions with Floodplain Management regulations, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and related environmental regulatory bodies.
Develop and maintain effective working relationships with staff, other state and federal agencies, environmental interests, industry professionals and local stakeholders.
Confer with permit applicants, developers, and consulting engineers via meetings, email, and formal correspondence; identify application deficiencies, recommend amendments, draft conditional approval or denial determinations, and prescribe necessary mitigation/follow-up actions.
Utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to process survey data, conduct spatial analyses, and generate cartographic products, spatial layers, and technical documentation for state parks, preserves, and public land management plans.
Maintain, enhance, and ensure data integrity of the Iowa Natural Areas Inventory (INAI) database; review, input, modify, and QC species location, population status, and community survey records.
Analyze field observations, biological data, and state/federal statutory requirements to evaluate ecological impacts and project viability and author comprehensive resource reports detailing plant and animal communities, habitat assessments, impact evaluations, and recommended land management practices.
Develop, read, and comprehend laws, rules, policies, technical documents and position papers and effectively communicate them orally and in writing.
Plan and perform comprehensive field surveys to locate, document, and evaluate rare, threatened, endangered, and sensitive species and natural plant/wildlife communities.

The Successful Candidate Must Be Able To

Produce quality work products in a timely manner.
Work independently with consistent results and minimal supervision.
Adjust to change, work pressures, or difficult situations without undue stress; some travel across the state as required.
Demonstrate initiative, a customer service focus and display high standards of ethical conduct.

Critical Job Competencies

Accountability, Integrity, High Productivity, Communication Skills, Team Player, Interpersonal Skills, Customer Focus, Self-Management, Technical Skills (GIS, Web-Based Applications)

What You Get From Us

A competitive pay plan and rewarding work.
Insurance benefits that start the first of the month following 30 days of employment. (Premiums can start as low as $64/month for single and $210/month for family coverage).
Separate vacation and sick leave accruals that start on the first day and can roll over annually.
Nine paid holidays/year.
Iowa Public Employee Retirement System (IPERS) retirement package with employer match.
Optional deferred compensation (457/401A) plan with employer match.
Professional training opportunities.
Family friendly and professional work environment.
Employee Discount Programs (vision, cellular, fitness, recreation, season passes, travel, counseling)
The State’s total compensation package features benefits that are worth about 30% of your total compensation. For a list of additional benefits, please visit the DAS website for more information.

Opportunities for hybrid telework (as approved by the supervisor).
Workout/Gym facilities available onsite at 6200 Park Ave.

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

Job Description

Position Summary:
The Courier is responsible for the pick-up and delivery of water, soil and air samples to and from the laboratory. Maintain the quality, hold time, and turnaround time objectives of the lab. Prepare and deliver bottle orders to clients following the standard operating procedures of the lab. Receive and stock all sample control supplies, prepare and ship sample kits and perform sampling events as needed. Dispose of samples and hazardous waste according to guidelines and carry out any other duties assigned by the department manager.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Perform all duties as outlined in the Standard Operating Procedures for Couriers.
Pick up and deliver samples, bottle orders and report to the laboratory for sign-in and analysis.
Count the number of samples when receiving them from clients to make sure that the Chain of Custody and samples match. Verify that samples are not broken or damaged.
Receive and sign the Chain of Custody.
Ensure that client signs, dates, and records time on the Chain of Custody when releasing samples.
Transport samples on ice from client site to the lab, or from our lab to a sub-contracted laboratory.
Unload samples and inspect for damage or violated hold times to maintain sample integrity.
Interact with Project Managers and clients appropriately and professionally.
Follow directions or use maps to locate client offices/sites as specified in the courier request form.
Communicate effectively with the courier coordinator about the courier schedule.
Record in the courier log book the time that courier arrives to the site and time leaving from the site for all the pick-ups and deliveries.
Maintain records for the vehicle maintenance and driving miles; turn it in at the end of each month.
Restock supplies when received so supplies are available to employees when needed.
Verify the validity and completeness of all bottle orders being delivered. This verification is done prior to leaving for delivery.
Perform duties in accordance with Section 14 of the Transportation and Fleet Safety of the Corporate Safety Manual.
Comply with the Company’s driver policies.
Maintain the shipping/receiving area to ensure a safe work environment.
Prepare outgoing shipments of bottle kits and coolers for pick-up.
Perform on-site sampling events as needed.
Dispose of samples according to guidelines on a monthly basis to remain in compliance with Environmental Protection Agency and Environmental Health & Safety requirements.
Maintain delivery truck to keep in proper working order.
Label samples after log in on an as needed basis.
May be assigned other sample control duties as identified by laboratory management.

Qualifications

Education/Experience (Basic Minimum Qualifications):

Education: High school diploma or equivalent

Experience: None required

Valid driver’s license

Ability and/or Skills (BMQ):

Reading maps and following directions
Operating a motor vehicle
Computer skills preferred
Ability to prioritize

Additional Information

Requirements:

Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

Position is full-time Monday - Friday 8am - 5pm. Candidates currently living within a commutable distance of Altamonte Springs, FL are encouraged to apply.

Position Purpose

The Senior Director of Environmental Compliance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of Veolia Water New Jersey’s (VWNJ) environmental compliance programs, ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, in alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities, while advancing public health protection, environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. This position provides executive oversight of all environmental compliance activities related to air, drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, waste management, hazardous materials, spill prevention and response, environmental permitting, emergency preparedness, and environmental auditing.

This position leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Company's environmental compliance management systems, environmental governance framework, and regulatory compliance programs across all VWNJ operations. The Senior Director provides oversight of all laboratory analysis required to demonstrate compliance, including outside laboratory services and the Haworth WTP laboratory.

The Senior Director serves as the organization's subject matter expert for environmental compliance, environmental permitting, drinking water quality, wastewater treatment compliance, environmental management systems, and environmental regulatory relations. The role partners closely with other functional areas including, operations, engineering, legal, finance, strategic relations, etc., to identify environmental risks, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure consistent compliance across all operations.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Lead, empower, and mentor a direct team of environmental professionals, driving cohesive collaboration and operational alignment across all functional disciplines within the position's scope (including Operations, Engineering, Legal, and Finance).
Serve as a strategic leader with external regulatory agencies, effectively interpreting complex regulations and guidelines to advocate for approaches that balance strict regulatory compliance with exceptional customer service and operational/business realities.
Provide environmental compliance leadership for VWNJ. Ensure alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Provide strategic oversight of compliance programs related to all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including requirements administered by the EPA and applicable state environmental agencies.
Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and communicate impacts to business leadership. Lead development of comments for submission during public comment period for draft regulatory requirements. Interpret emerging regulatory requirements and develop implementation strategies to ensure organizational readiness.
Support development of policies related to water treatment operations, laboratory quality assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of VWNJ’s environmental compliance management systems.
Lead environmental due diligence activities supporting capital projects and new business initiatives.
Evaluate environmental impacts associated with operational activities and infrastructure investments.
Direct internal environmental assessments and support external regulatory inspections. Oversee development, implementation, and closure of corrective action plans.
Lead VWNJ environmental auditing and compliance assurance programs.
Monitor environmental performance trends and ensure timely resolution of compliance issues.
Oversee environmental permitting activities across all operations.
Ensure timely submission of required regulatory reports and environmental compliance documentation.
Ensure maintenance of systems supporting environmental permits, compliance obligations, inspections, reporting, and regulatory commitments.
Provide oversight of environmental emergency preparedness and response programs.
Direct environmental incident investigations, including spill response and root cause analyses.
Serve as liaison with environmental regulatory agencies.
Build productive relationships with regulators, industry associations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the organization during inspections, audits, enforcement actions, and compliance negotiations.
Establish departmental goals, performance expectations, succession planning, and employee development initiatives.
Allocate resources to support business priorities and regulatory obligations.
Foster collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Legal,Finance, and Corporate leadership.
Develop departmental strategic plans, budgets, and resource forecasts.
Establish and monitor environmental performance objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting metrics.
Recommend process improvements that enhance compliance, operational reliability, sustainability, and financial performance.
Support corporate sustainability and environmental stewardship initiatives.

Work Environment

Participation in environmental emergency response activities and on-call leadership, as required.
Combination of office and field environments, including visits to treatment facilities, construction sites, laboratories, and industrial operations.
Ability to conduct field inspections and work in varying environmental conditions while utilizing appropriate personal protective equipment.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or a related technical discipline.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 12 years of progressively responsible environmental compliance experience within a regulated utility, environmental services, industrial, manufacturing, or infrastructure organization.
Minimum of 7 years of leadership experience managing environmental professionals and cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated experience leading environmental compliance programs across multiple operating locations.
Experience interacting with federal and state regulatory agencies.
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance management systems.
Experience supporting environmental due diligence, capital projects, and business development preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Safe Drinking Water Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Clean Air Act, and related environmental permitting requirements.
Knowledge of drinking water treatment, water chemistry, wastewater operations, hazardous materials management, and environmental risk management.
Strong understanding of environmental auditing, compliance assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience developing environmental compliance strategies, policies, and governance frameworks.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build effective relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong project management and organizational leadership capabilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Google applications and environmental compliance management systems.

Additional Information

Pay Range:
$180000 to $200000 Per Year.

Benefits:
Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement. Pay and benefits for employees represented by a union are outlined in their collective bargaining agreement.

Sick leave – 56 hours; Observed Holidays – 11 days; Vacation – Flexible Time Off

Eligible for up to 20% Annual Performance Bonus

Job Description

Expression of Interest - Engineers | Technicians | Project Managers | Environmental Scientists

Bring your expertise. Build something meaningful— and a great life — in Bundaberg.

Are you an experienced technical or project professional looking for greater influence, meaningful regional work and the opportunity to grow your leadership career?

Join GHD’s close-knit Bundaberg team and help shape projects that support communities across the Wide Bay. You’ll enjoy the visibility and connection of a regional office, backed by the capability, opportunities and multidisciplinary expertise of GHD’s wider Queensland and global network.

GHD is seeking Expressions of Interest
from experienced professionals interested in joining our Bundaberg team and leading our growth and presence across the Wide Bay region.

We’re deliberately keeping our search broad. Your project management or technical background could be in transport, civil, water, structural, electrical, environment or another technical discipline. What matters most is your ability to bring strong consulting experience, work closely with clients and contribute to both project delivery and business growth.

Build your career, and a great life, in Bundaberg

A move to Bundaberg could mean creating more space for what matters while continuing to work on meaningful projects, build trusted client relationships and grow your professional influence.

Bundaberg combines the serenity of coastal living with a strong sense of community and connection. The region is the closest mainland gateway to Lady Musgrave and Lady Elliot islands — two of the Southern Great Barrier Reef’s finest coral cays — and is surrounded by beaches, mangroves, and other ecosystems that support diverse marine life.

The region also offers the everyday essentials that make relocation easier: accessibility to Brisbane, modern schools, growing recreational opportunities, and high-quality healthcare facilities and upgrades. A diversified regional economy supports employment, investment and a lifestyle that guarantees a rewarding alternative to the hustle and bustle of major-city living.

At GHD, you’ll become part of a close-knit local team where your contribution will be visible and valued. You’ll work alongside people with deep regional knowledge while being widely supported by multidisciplinary colleagues across Queensland and GHD’s global network. It’s an opportunity to build local relationships, broaden your experience and make a lasting impact on the communities around you.

Discover what life in the Bundaberg region could offer you.

What could your opportunity look like?

Depending on your experience and background, you could join us as an Engineer, Technician, Project Manager or Environmental Scientist. In our Bundaberg team, you’ll have the opportunity to work across disciplines, build strong relationships with regional clients and play a visible role in the continued growth of our Wide Bay business.

Regional consulting can offer broader exposure and greater influence. You may find yourself working more closely with clients, contributing across the full project lifecycle and helping shape opportunities from their earliest stages — while still having access to the technical depth and career pathways of a global professional services company.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

This opportunity isn’t defined by a single technical discipline. We’re looking for the right capability, consulting mindset and client orientation to complement our Bundaberg team and contribute to our continued growth across the region.

What You’ll Bring

We’d like to hear from you if you bring:

5 plus years’ experience in consulting, technical delivery or project management
A background in engineering, environment, project management or another relevant technical discipline
Strong client-facing and relationship-building capability
A commercial mindset and an interest in identifying and developing opportunities
The ability and willingness to contribute directly to project delivery
A collaborative approach and the ability to work across disciplines, projects and locations
An interest in contributing to the continued growth of our Bundaberg business
The ambition to continue developing your career and potentially move into broader leadership over time
Relevant professional accreditation for your discipline, such as RPEQ and/or CPEng, or working towards attaining accreditation where applicable

You don’t need to already know the Queensland market. We’re interested in professionals who bring the right consulting and client-focused approach, valuable experience and a willingness to collaborate with colleagues who have strong local market knowledge.

Why GHD?

At GHD, you’ll have the opportunity to combine your technical expertise, project experience and client relationships while being connected to a broader multidisciplinary business.

This isn’t about fitting into a narrowly defined role. We’re interested in what you could bring to Bundaberg.

Whether you’re an experienced engineer, project manager, technical specialist or consultant looking for greater influence, broader client exposure and an opportunity to contribute to regional growth, we’d like to hear from you.

Could Bundaberg be your next move?

Register your interest and start a confidential conversation with us about your experience, career goals and what life and work with GHD in Bundaberg could look like. Explore the region at bundabergregion.org.

GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces a range of flexible work practices to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.

About Us

Come together and make a meaningful impact.

We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD.

Let's drive real change.

Our Pledge to You

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

That’s the #PowerOfCommitment

Who We Are

GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.

The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

About EHS Support

EHS Support is a specialty environmental consulting firm that provides solutions to complex environmental, health, and safety challenges across a range of market sectors and industries. With experts located throughout the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and South Africa, we form long-lasting partnerships with our clients through a culture of excellence, innovation, work ethic, and integrity. We focus on hiring and retaining talented, motivated people who enjoy collaborating with and delivering value to our clients. Our team does more than identify problems— we provide solutions.

Location:

Brisbane, QLD - flexible home, office and field-based role

About The Role

We are seeking an experienced environmental scientist or engineer to join our Queensland team and play a leading role in the delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.

This role is suited to an experienced consultant who enjoys technical problem solving, project leadership and working with clients to develop practical and defensible environmental solutions. The position offers exposure to a broad range of projects and sectors, including energy, resources, infrastructure, manufacturing, chemicals and heavy industry.

While a strong background in contaminated land assessment and management is important, we are particularly interested in adaptable practitioners who can apply their technical skills across a range of environmental disciplines, including compliance, approvals, environmental due diligence, environmental management and remediation.

The preferred location for this role is Brisbane; however, other Queensland locations will be considered for suitably experienced candidates. The role involves a flexible mix of office, home and field-based work, together with periodic travel to project sites throughout Queensland and Australia.

Typical Responsibilities

Lead technical delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
Plan, coordinate and manage environmental investigations, including soil, groundwater, surface water and vapour assessment programs.
Review, interpret and evaluate environmental data and develop technically robust and commercially practical recommendations.
Author and review technical reports and project deliverables, including:
Preliminary and detailed site investigations
Contaminated land assessments
Remediation action plans and validation reports
Environmental management plans
Compliance and monitoring report
Environmental approvals and supporting documentation
Provide technical leadership and quality assurance for work completed by project team members.
Lead the technical delivery and project execution of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
Coordinate and supervise subcontractors and specialist service providers during field investigations and remediation works.
Engage directly with clients, regulators, contractors and other stakeholders to support project delivery and resolve technical issues.
Contribute to proposal preparation, scope development and cost estimation for new opportunities.
Support the development of junior and intermediate staff through technical guidance, coaching and project leadership.
Contribute to technical innovation and continuous improvement initiatives within the business.

As a growing business, this role provides opportunities to expand technical leadership responsibilities, strengthen client relationships, contribute to service development and play a meaningful role in the continued growth of the Queensland practice.

Position Requirements

This opportunity is suited to a motivated and adaptable environmental professional who combines strong technical capability with project leadership and client management skills. The successful candidate will demonstrate:

Strong technical knowledge of contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental management principles.
Excellent analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to develop practical and defensible solutions to complex environmental challenges.
Exceptional written communication skills and demonstrated experience preparing high-quality technical reports and client deliverables.
Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
Proven ability to manage projects, coordinate multidisciplinary teams and deliver successful outcomes.
Ability to work independently while providing leadership and direction within collaborative project teams.
Sound professional judgement and a practical approach to balancing technical, regulatory and commercial considerations.
A strong commitment to health, safety and environmental performance.

Qualifications For This Role Include

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Soil Science, Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or a related discipline.
Approximately 7-10 years' experience in environmental consulting or a closely related technical role.
Demonstrated experience undertaking and managing contaminated land investigations, environmental site assessments and remediation projects.
Strong understanding of the ASC NEPM and Queensland contaminated land regulatory framework.
Experience managing environmental field programs, including soil, groundwater and surface water investigations.
Demonstrated experience leading the preparation and review of high-quality technical reports and client deliverables.
Proven project management experience, including management of scope, schedule, budget and project risks.
Experience working across multiple environmental service areas such as compliance, approvals, environmental management, due diligence or remediation would be highly regarded.
Current Australian driver's licence and the ability to work in Australia.

At EHS Support, we’re passionate about creating a workplace where our people feel valued, supported, and inspired. We empower our team to deliver innovative, practical solutions for our clients and the environment, while continuously growing their careers in a collaborative and forward‑thinking environment.

jobs.description:
About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

A Junior Environmental Scientist
participates as a member of an emergency response team to conduct environmental sampling and data collection. In performing such duties, a Junior Environmental Scientist will conduct research or perform investigations for the purpose of identifying, abating, or eliminating sources of pollutants or hazards that affect either the environment or the health of the population. Utilizing their knowledge of various scientific disciplines, they may collect, synthesize, study, report, and act based on data derived from measurements or observations of air, food, soil, water, and other sources. The successful candidate will apply scientific methodology for analysis of risk assessments and industrial hygiene applications to ensure the client’s expectations are met. All Junior Environmental Scientist’s shall maintain a response bag with company issued PPE and appropriate work clothing. This role is also subject to on-call rotation for emergency response and frequent, extended travel. The on-call rotation duties may extend to satellite offices as necessary. Travel on a moment’s notice may extend further than just the on-call rotation i.e. in the event a response requires more staffing support.

The compensation range for this role is $38,500 to $44,600
commensurate with experience, skills, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

Immediate availability for extended travel and emergency response at client’s request
Maintain, calibrate and mobilize equipment appropriate for an emergency response
Gather and analyze samples from various sources of potential contamination
Perform monitoring and sampling activities according to the prescribed methods
Compile, review and summarize scientific/technical data and literature; and,
Completion of 40-hour HAZWOPER training in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.120 within first three weeks of hire date
Possession of DISA & TWIC clearances within 3 months of hire date
Completion of all designated safety requirements within first month of hire date; and
Perform other duties as assigned

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

Bachelor's degree in Biology, Environmental Engineering, Environmental, Health and Safety,
Industrial Hygiene, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Toxicology or other related science

, you are responsible for leading all manufacturing plant personnel in all aspects of environmental, safety, health, security, and training. The responsibilities include actively participating in and supporting the environmental safety and health initiatives established by ICL, leading continual improvement in the facilities Responsible Care EHS management systems, participating in internal EHSS compliance audits, meeting business commitments, managing EHS elements of capital project design and providing effective internal and external communication.

I’m interested! What will I get to do in this position?

Ensure ESH compliance through working closely with corporate ESH, Production, and Quality personnel
Serve as a liaison with local, state, and federal representatives from regulatory agencies including IOSHA, EPA, IDEM, DOT and local emergency responders
Oversee submission of permit applications (air and/or water and/or waste) and reports as required by environmental regulations
Initiate and manage capital projects supporting the environmental safety and health initiatives established by ICL
Lead continual improvement of the Responsible Care 14001 EHS Management System
Lead site implementation of global EHS tools including Enablon and GOARC
Evaluate EHS impacts for change management throughout operations
Provide facility EHS focus through the development and completion of annual EHSS workplan plans and support JHAs, and EHS inspections/audits
Lead and participate in Process Hazard Analyses, including HAZOP, What-if, etc.
Develop, conduct, and evaluate required EHS training for all employees
Ensure accurate EHS record keeping (e.g., medical records, OSHA Log, WC)
Drive culture of early detection of hazardous and learning from events to build defenses and minimize incidents
Actively participate on the ICL North America regional EHS team and auditing program
Interact with outside vendors that are directly involved with compliance efforts including Environmental, Insurance and other outside services

BS or BA degree in Environmental Health & Safety or a related degree
A minimum of 2 years of EHS experience preferred
Knowledge in Process Safety Management preferred
Experience in managing people/processes in health and safety field
Strong organization/leadership skills
Previous management experience in an industrial and chemical manufacturing environment preferred
Proficient with MS Office
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively interact with all levels of the organization

What will set me apart?

Project Management
Experience with Enablon EHSS management system

: $69,000-$85,000

Take the lead in driving innovation

At Volvo Cars, we are committed to advancing safety, sustainability and electrification. To achieve our ambitious goals, we are looking for forward-thinking individuals who can identify challenges before they arise and deliver cutting-edge solutions that set new industry standards.

When you choose a career with Volvo Cars, you’re not just joining a company – you’re helping shape the future of mobility.

Let's introduce ourselves

The role of the Sr. Environmental Specialist
will play a key role in the coordination of work and the forwarding of environmental issues within the Volvo Cars Charleston manufacturing plant in Ridgeville, SC. This position will support/lead the environmental areas of responsibility in relation to air and water emissions, waste management, as well as the implementation and oversight of ISO 14001, Volvo’s environmental management system. Volvo is a world-class automotive manufacturer with a uniquely strong focus on reducing its inherent impact on the environment. jobs.description:
Job Title:
Risk Assessor II

Location:
Lakewood, CO

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is seeking a Risk Assessor II to support environmental projects, including hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste; PFAS; mining; and military munitions response program projects nationwide. The Risk Assessor II will prepare human health risk assessments and/or ecological risk assessments in accordance with CERCLA, RCRA, and applicable state guidance, with support from HGL’s risk assessment team, including senior- and principal-level staff. The ideal candidate can lead both human health and ecological risk assessments; candidates with strong experience in either discipline will also be considered. This role is well suited for a self-directed individual who enjoys integrating complex environmental data, technical analysis, and regulatory requirements to support sound project and remedial decisions. HGL is seeking to fill one hybrid position based out of our Denver office in Lakewood, CO.

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Manage and analyze large environmental datasets.
Prepare tables, figures, and other data exhibits.
Author risk assessments, risk assessment work plans, and other technical deliverables.
Review and interpret environmental and toxicological studies and reports.
Support remedial strategy design, including development of risk-based cleanup levels.
Conduct statistical analyses, including statistical comparisons of background data to site data.
Serve as the project risk assessor in project meetings and technical discussions with clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders.
Lead and provide technical direction to junior-level staff.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

Bachelor’s degree in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
At least 6 years of work experience in an environmental consulting or regulatory environment on DoD or EPA projects, with a focus on site investigation and human health or ecological risk assessment; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience implementing EPA’s Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund and/or EPA’s Ecological Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund.
Working knowledge of relevant federal regulations, especially CERCLA and RCRA, and the ability to integrate federal requirements with varying state regulations.
Ability to present technical information effectively to scientific, regulatory, and public audiences.
Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, manage multiple project assignments, meet strict deadlines, travel to client facilities as needed, and work independently as a self-starter.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Advanced degree (MS, MPH, or PhD) in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
Experience completing statistical comparisons of site data to background data and geochemical evaluations to distinguish site-related contaminants from background constituents.
Experience in technical areas beyond risk assessment—such as contaminant fate and transport, analytical chemistry, characterization of the nature and extent of contamination, or development of remediation strategies—to support integration across project teams.
Experience designing and leading baseline ecological risk assessments that include collection of site-specific data, such as biota tissue, toxicity testing, bioaccumulation studies, or habitat and/or species surveys.
Experience in blood lead modeling to support human health risk assessments.
Familiarity with environmental databases, primarily LOCUS, and statistical software.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIREMENTS

Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time.
Viewing computer screen for extended periods.
Analyzing and synthesizing data.
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities.

Work Environment Requirements

Office work environment.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

Work Schedule:
HGL office work is dictated by a 5-day work week; however, fieldwork schedules will deviate based on job requirements and may require longer hours and weekends.

Office Type:
Hybrid (3 days in office)

Travel:
Minimal but as needed to client facilities; percentage varies by project assignment.

A favorable pre-hire drug test is required.

All positions are subject to a pre-hire education and driving record verification.

MORE ABOUT HGL AND THE OPPORTUNITY

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. We believe that we can make a difference in improving the world we live in through collaboration, teamwork, and a positive work environment. This unites and empowers us to strive for excellence in all our endeavors.

Hgl - Who We Are

The exceptional quality of our people is key to our strength. We value our employees as individuals and as important members of our team. We offer a work environment that is flexible, inclusive, and dedicated to creating a sustainable future. By cultivating a culture of innovation, we’re able to adapt and augment our services to solve complex environmental and natural resources challenges.

Projects at HGL primarily span the United States and its territories, tackling problems associated with emerging contaminants (like PFAS), radiological contamination, and military munitions, along with chemical contamination in groundwater, surface water, sediments, and soil.

With over 550 employees, HGL is large enough to execute high-profile projects, but small enough to develop personal working environments with our talented team members. By joining HGL, you will be working toward restoring the environment and protecting our future.

HGL - WE INVEST IN YOU

It’s not just a job, it’s your career. HGL provides career growth opportunities via mentoring, training, education, and support for your certifications and licenses. Achieve your career goals and help HGL achieve its mission of restoring the environment to beneficial use for our clients and communities.
