jobs.description:
Dallas is Growing. Grow With Us.

Looking for more than just a job? The City of Dallas offers careers with purpose. With competitive benefits, growth opportunities, and a vibrant work culture,

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Job Summary

Under minimum to no supervision, performs complex environmental work. Inspects public and private facilities, indoor and outdoor sites, and investigates incidents to determine compliance with environmental laws and regulations. Works independently and is responsible for making decisions requiring technical discretion, sound judgement, and specialized knowledge.

Overview

Job Description

The Environmental Specialist III conducts inspections and investigations of public and private sites to ensure compliance with environmental laws and standards. Responds to review requests, prepares detailed reports, supports audits through site visits and documents reviews, and collects and analyzes environmental samples. The role also includes managing hazardous waste disposal, assisting with document control, and supporting interdepartmental investigations and water quality programs.

Essential Functions

1 Travels through the City of Dallas to inspect and evaluate various public and private facilities utilizing ISO standards; performs complex environmental evaluations, inspections, and reviews city services and utilities; investigates complaints, and files compliance reports for environmental agencies. Conducts water quality monitoring and sampling, collects grab samples, preserves sample integrity, records field results, and prepares samples for laboratory analysis to meet program requirements.

2 Oversees, monitors, and provides experience-based skill for cleaning spills and other potentially hazardous situations affecting the MS4; ensures spills are cleaned appropriately, investigates causes of incidents to determine preventability, and ensures incident reports are filed accordingly.

3 Inspects public and private sites and indoor/outdoor facilities for environmental compliance; reviews waste storage areas, workplace chemical lists, water facilities, SCBA equipment, stormwater management tactics, permits, and other water activities; observes and identifies issues, mitigates and follows through the resolution of the identified issues.

4 Reviews and files extensive data-driven reports on inspections, service requests and spill response activities; documents areas of non-compliance, produces preventable reports, makes recommendations on various incidents; ensures all relevant parties are aware of issues and have comprehensive data to make informed decisions; provides follow-ups on compliance investigations. Tracks and maintains inventory of environmental spill response supplies.

5 Applies and enforces environmental policies, rules, regulations, and standards to meet and exceed expectations set by the City of Dallas; provides training and continuous education to other employees to ensure all inspection and compliance activities are completed efficiently.

6 Responds to 24-hour emergency service requests and assists with reports for Environmental Compliance Committee meetings.

7 Reviews permits and regulations regarding various industries and monitors compliance with permitting standards.

8 Maintains compliance with Federal, State and local regulations of a waste storage facility. Supports operations of the generation and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste accumulated by Dallas Fire & Rescue (DFR) and the Stormwater Compliance response team, when necessary. Performs daily operations and required inspections of the Stormwater

Compliance Waste Yard. Conducts deliveries of environmental spill remediation supplies to all DFR fire stations.

9 Performs other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge and Skills

1 Thorough knowledge of environmental compliance regulations, such as The Clean Water Act (CWA) and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA).

2 Thorough knowledge of environmental procedures and inspection tactics, such as RG-416 Surface Water Monitoring Procedures (Bio Program) and RG-415 TCEQ Surface WQ Monitoring Procedures (Physical & Chemical Monitoring).

3 Expert knowledge of environmental codes, ordinances, and regulations, such as Texas Water Quality Standards.

4 Expertise in performing professional inspections and documenting non-compliance findings.

5 Skill in resolving findings and ensuring issue closure.

6 Skill in developing training materials and educating other specialists and citizens.

7 Ability to provide engagement and follow up to ensure environmental standards are achieved.

8 Advanced skill in communicating effectively both verbally and in writing.

9 Advanced skills in Power BI, GIS, and Excel.

10 Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Experience

Five (5) years of hands-on experience in performing environmental inspections, handling hazardous materials, performing chemical analysis in waste management, spill response or soil/water/air/groundwater sample collection environment.

Licenses and Certifications

Valid driver’s license and good driving record.

A forty (40)-hr HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) certification is required for all spill response divisions.

For Stormwater Neighborhood and Water Reservoir divisions, Registered Environmental Manager (REM) certification is required.

For Stormwater Neighborhood division, a Certified Environmental Storm Water Compliance Professional (CESCP) certification and a Boater Certificate are required.

For Water Quality division, a Boater Certificate and a Class D (or higher) Water license from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) are required.

Education

High School or GED with a study course in sciences, chemistry or biology.

Preferred

OSHA 30-hour Safety Certificate is preferred.
Experience with ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems certified programs is highly preferred.
Experience with maintaining/using Safety Data Sheets (SDS) is preferred.
Experience with inspecting storm sewer/drainage structures (e.g., MS4, outfalls, storm sewer pipe, inlets, wing walls, culverts, junctions, etc.) is preferred.
Experience with Stormwater Permits (Construction General Permit TXR150000 and the Multi Sector General Permit TXR 050000) and Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) are preferred for certain divisions.

Equivalency

An associate degree in chemistry, engineering, environmental or physical sciences field plus three (3) years of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

A bachelor's degree (or higher) in chemistry, environmental or natural sciences field, and one (1) year of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

Other Requirements

Must pass background investigation. No Felony convictions. Cannot currently be on deferred adjudication for any Felony, Class A or Class B Misdemeanor. Availability to work varying shifts including nights, weekends, and holidays. Subject to twenty-four (24) hour call-out. Working conditions include potential exposure to bio-hazardous material(s), hazardous chemicals, inclement weather, and confined spaces.

Salary Range

$25.12 - $28.85

The salary listed on this job posting is the starting salary range; amount offered will depend upon qualifications.

City of Dallas is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Environmental Remediation Project Manager, Senior

The Opportunity:

Delivers senior-level project management and technical advising services for Department of War (DOW) environmental clients. Advises on environmental program planning, programming, budgeting, scheduling, management, execution, and contract surveillance. Assist clients in managing complex remediation sites involving contaminated soil, sediment, surface water, and groundwater. Applies technical expertise in geology, hydrogeology, remedy design, or risk assessment for environmental site characterization and remediation. Analyzes regulatory, policy, and guidance requirements, evaluates environmental data, and develops actionable investigation and remediation strategies. Reviews environmental restoration documents, supports contracting activities and stakeholder meetings, oversees fieldwork, and mentors junior staff.

You Have:

15+ years of experience technical environmental or project management roles, specialized within investigation and remediation or restoration program areas under CERCLA
Experience in managing complex projects for environmental sites under state regulatory, RCRA, or CERCLA programs
Knowledge of emerging contaminants, including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
Ability to work alongside the DoW, client agency, state and local government agencies, stakeholders under state regulations, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), or Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)
Ability to provide technical document reviews and comments for environmental investigations, remediation, and site closure work plans and reports
Ability to perform or conduct oversight of environmental field activities, such as excavation, drilling, well installation, sampling, or remedial systems installation
Ability to travel throughout the U.S., including Alaska, up to 25% of the time to support DoW clients at various installations
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust or Suitability/Fitness determination based on client requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, or Toxicology
40-hour Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) certification

Experience in environmental consulting and project management including engaging directly with Department of Air Force clients
Ability to pay strict attention to detail for analysis
Possession of excellent time management, strategic thinking, organizational, and verbal and written communication skills
Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, Toxicology, or Business Administration
Professional Engineer (PE) license, Professional Geologist (PG) license, Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM) certification, Registered Environmental Manager (REM), and Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

AE2S is seeking an experienced and motivated Environmental Scientist II to join our growing environmental team. Prepare and manage environmental permitting, regulatory compliance documentation, environmental assessments, mitigation plans, technical reports, and agency correspondence.
Interpret and apply local, state, and federal environmental regulations, coordinating directly with regulatory agencies to support project approvals and compliance requirements.
Analyze environmental data and evaluate project impacts, developing avoidance, minimization, mitigation, restoration, and monitoring strategies.

Contribute to business growth by participating in client meetings, proposal development, scope preparation, fee estimates, and relationship-building opportunities.

Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines while maintaining high-quality technical work.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to work effectively with clients, regulatory agencies, and project teams.

Ability to stand or sit for prolonged periods of time

jobs.description:
Job Title: Environmental Scientist
Job Description

The Environmental Scientist will support remediation and environmental compliance projects, with a strong focus on Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and field sampling of soil and water. The role involves planning and executing fieldwork, analyzing environmental data, and preparing clear, well-structured technical reports with minimal supervision. This position offers an excellent opportunity to gain broad project experience and build a long-term career in environmental consulting.

Responsibilities

Conduct Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, including site inspections, records reviews, and documentation of findings.
Perform field sampling activities for soil and water in accordance with established protocols and regulatory requirements.
Support remediation and environmental compliance projects by collecting, organizing, and interpreting environmental data.
Prepare clear, concise, and technically accurate site assessment and project reports with minimal supervision.
Ensure that all field and office work complies with applicable environmental regulations, guidelines, and company procedures.
Assist with environmental site assessments for a variety of properties and facilities, including potentially complex or regulated sites.
Collaborate effectively with project teams to plan fieldwork, coordinate logistics, and meet project deadlines.
Apply critical thinking to identify potential environmental concerns and recommend appropriate next steps or further investigations.
Communicate findings and technical information in a clear written format suitable for clients, regulators, and internal stakeholders.
Demonstrate leadership potential by taking ownership of assigned tasks and contributing to a disciplined, hard-working team culture.

Essential Skills

13 years of experience as a geologist or environmental scientist working on environmental projects.
Hands-on experience conducting Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
Demonstrated soil sampling experience in the field.
Demonstrated water sampling experience in the field.
Knowledge of remediation practices and environmental compliance requirements.
Ability to complete site reports and technical documentation with minimal supervision.
Strong written communication skills for clear, professional report writing.
Scientific degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Chemistry, Biology, or a related field.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification.
Experience with environmental site assessments beyond Phase I, including work at landfills or similar sites.
Background or coursework in environmental science, geology, or related environmental disciplines.
Strong critical thinking skills and the ability to analyze complex environmental information.
Demonstrated leadership ability and willingness to take initiative on projects.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team and contribute to a collaborative work environment.
Clear and concise writing style suitable for technical and non-technical audiences.

Work Environment

The work environment combines office-based report preparation with fieldwork at various sites, including properties undergoing environmental assessment or remediation. The organization operates with a strong family-oriented culture and a smaller, close-knit team rather than a large corporate structure. Leadership remains actively involved in project work, fostering a hands-on, supportive atmosphere. Team members are driven, disciplined, and hard-working, and the company seeks individuals who share these values and want to build a long-term career in environmental consulting.

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Birmingham, AL.

jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a commercially focused, strategic, and results-driven Sales Development Manager to lead growth within the rapidly expanding PFAS testing market across the United States.

The successful candidate will drive market development and revenue growth by partnering with Contract Testing Organizations (CTOs), environmental laboratories, commercial analytical testing providers, and strategic industry stakeholders. The role will focus on positioning Waters PFAS analytical solutions, workflows, applications, consumables, informatics, and services to enable laboratories to expand testing capacity, improve productivity, and respond to evolving regulatory requirements.

This role requires close collaboration with regional sales teams, application specialists, marketing, regulatory affairs, and business units to identify growth opportunities and develop strategic commercial plans that accelerate Waters leadership in PFAS analysis. This is a remote position based in the United States with significant customer-facing engagement.

Responsibilities

Market Development, Strategy and Opportunity Creation

Develop and execute the U.S. PFAS CTO growth strategy, including market segmentation, geographic prioritization, target-account planning and opportunity creation.
Identify opportunities across environmental, water, food, packaging, cosmetics, textiles and industrial materials testing laboratories, informed by regulatory drivers, market trends and competitive dynamics.
Build relationships with key decision-makers, laboratory leaders, industry influencers and strategic customer stakeholders.

Pipeline Development, Commercial Execution and Sales Support

Generate, qualify and manage a robust PFAS opportunity pipeline through customer engagement, networking, conferences, campaigns and targeted outreach.
Partner with account managers, specialists and application scientists to progress opportunities through evaluations, demonstrations, workflow discussions, proposals and commercial negotiations.
Maintain accurate forecasts and coordinate executive-level engagement for strategic customer accounts.

Customer Relationship Management and Strategic Partnerships

Develop trusted-advisor relationships with contract testing organizations, laboratory networks and senior customer stakeholders.
Support laboratory growth discussions by connecting PFAS market trends, workflow optimization and Waters solution value propositions.
Capture customer feedback and unmet needs to inform strategy, product development and customer success initiatives.

Sales Enablement, Marketing and Demand Generation

Enable field teams on PFAS regulations, workflows, technologies, competitive positioning and customer value propositions.
Partner with marketing to execute lead-generation initiatives, webinars, workshops, conferences, customer events and digital campaigns focused on the contract testing market.
Support customer stories, co-authored technical content and industry thought leadership that increase Waters visibility and demand.

Technical, Regulatory and Market Expertise

Maintain strong knowledge of PFAS workflows, LC-MS/MS, LC-HRMS, sample preparation, automation, informatics and emerging screening approaches.
Monitor PFAS regulations, testing requirements, methods and laboratory accreditation expectations affecting the U.S. testing market.
Translate complex technical, regulatory and market information into actionable commercial plans and value propositions for scientific and commercial audiences.

Business Analytics, Reporting and Cross-Functional Collaboration

Provide regular updates on market conditions, competitive activity, pipeline progression, revenue performance and strategic recommendations to business leadership.
Use CRM and data-driven analysis to manage opportunities, improve forecasting and guide resource prioritization.
Collaborate across sales, marketing, application support, service, regulatory affairs, product management and business leadership to coordinate PFAS growth initiatives and share best practices globally.

Qualifications
Experience
Skills and Competencies
Commercial Strategy and Market Development
Relationship Building, Influence and Communication
Technical, Regulatory and Laboratory Expertise

Education
Bachelor degree in Chemistry, Environmental Science, Analytical Science, Biology, or a related scientific discipline.
Advanced scientific degree (MSc or PhD) and/or MBA preferred.
Minimum 5 years of experience in scientific sales, business development, market development, or commercial leadership.
Experience working within PFAS, environmental testing, analytical instrumentation, laboratory services, or regulated testing markets.
Demonstrated success building new market opportunities and influencing complex purchasing decisions.
Experience engaging with contract testing organizations, environmental laboratories, CROs, or commercial laboratory networks highly desirable.
Experience utilizing CRM systems such as Salesforce for opportunity management and forecasting.
Ability to develop and execute market expansion strategies, build business cases and identify emerging market opportunities.
Strong business acumen with a focus on growth, revenue generation and commercial execution.
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to assess market trends, regulatory developments and competitive positioning, translating insight into actionable commercial plans.
Proven ability to establish strong relationships with customers, business leaders and technical stakeholders.
Excellent networking, negotiation and stakeholder management capabilities, with the ability to influence without direct authority across cross-functional teams.
Outstanding written, verbal and presentation skills, with confidence engaging laboratory scientists, executives, regulators and commercial teams at conferences, workshops, customer meetings and executive reviews.
Strong understanding of analytical chemistry, PFAS testing workflows, LC-MS/MS technologies and environmental laboratory operations.
Familiarity with EPA methods, regulatory testing programs and laboratory accreditation requirements is highly desirable.
Ability to translate technical and regulatory complexity into clear customer value propositions and practical commercial guidance.

Extraordinary Teams Building Inspiring Projects

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations.

Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report.

Project Overview

Bechtel’s Manufacturing and Technology (M&T) Business Unit is designing, building and commissioning a semiconductor fab in Clay, NY. M&T is an exciting and growing business unit that serves customers in the semiconductor, datacenter, life sciences, and electric vehicle markets. M&T strives to exceed our customer objectives through utilizing our agility, innovative technologies, and world class talent. M&T solves the industry's toughest challenges, building both our company and the world for the future. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, the M&T global business unit also includes colleagues working in Arizona, Ohio, Texas, India, and additional project locations around the world.

Job Summary

The Senior Environmental Scientist helps develop and execute the environmental component of an Environmental, Safety, and Health (ESH) program. Key activities involve administrative and field tasks per established industry practices, procedures, and regulatory and Bechtel requirements. The position involves practical application of biology, ecology, chemistry, social sciences, and related disciplines for managing environmental aspects of a project or facility. The position reports to an Environmental Manager or ESH Manager

Major Responsibilities

Integrate environmental requirements into project planning, permitting, design, construction, commissioning and startup, and operations.
Provide support in the execution of environmental permits, plans, and assessments.
Monitor, and enforce environmental requirements for subcontractors, including onboarding, field verification, and corrective action management.
Perform site assessments and survey to identify site conditions and develop mitigation and sustainability strategies to protect the environment and local communities.
Provide technical guidance and support regarding mitigation measures pertaining to natural and cultural resources and communities.
Support environmental risk management associated with hazardous chemicals, high-purity systems, and simultaneous construction and owner activities typical of semiconductor fabrication facilities.
Provides technical assistance within ESH teams and to other project groups regarding permitting, risk assessment, plan preparation, studies, and ESH program execution.
Identify and track environmental issues, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder concerns.
Participate in emergency response, and aids investigation and resolution of ESH incidents.
Perform environmental monitoring, sampling, and inspections to confirm compliance with permits and project requirements and commitments.
Prepare training documents and help with ESH training for project/facility employees and visitors.
Participate in meetings with customers, project team members, and contractors and subcontractors to advise them of environmental requirements that may affect their work.
Assist other ESH team members in program execution, inclusive of safety and health.

Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) related to environmental sciences, field biology, or natural resources and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree

Required Knowledge And Skills

Bachelor of Science degree (or equivalent) from an accredited university or college in an applicable technical discipline such as environmental science, ecology, biology, natural resources, or related disciplines.
Five or more years of experience related to applicable environmental sciences or regulatory requirements.
Experience supporting semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or similar complex industrial projects is preferred.
Ability to evaluate environmental risk and apply sound judgment in fast-paced, high-consequence construction environments.
Ability to communicate environmental risks and requirements clearly to project leadership and client representatives.
Experience with environmental impact assessments.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Proficiency with computers for presentations, data management, and reports.
Analytical skills related to sampling, monitoring, and recordkeeping.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions and support multiple shifts.
Valid driver’s license.
Additional Qualifications

Demonstrated interest, training, and experience in applied sciences.

Knowledge and experience with ISO 14001 Management System standards.

Specialized technical skills and knowledge related to an applicable environmental discipline.

Broad technical knowledge, science skills, and technical writing abilities.

Total Rewards/Benefits

jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.

The position offers learning and growth opportunities for a professional seeking to develop a career in the environmental industry as an environmental scientist with a focus on natural resource studies and contamination evaluations. The position will be a technical support role under the guidance and leadership of seasoned professionals and industry thought leaders. Our group offers a diverse base of technical expertise to provide opportunities to offer professionals the ability to specialize and advance skills. This is an excellent opportunity to join an environmental team, apply your environmental skills, and contribute technically to infrastructure projects that are recognized at the federal, state, and local levels and have tremendous public benefits. Our work includes research, field studies, reporting, presentations, mapping, permit applications, data analysis, regulatory reviews, and interactions with many engineering and environmental disciplines. Join our team!

As an Associate Environmental Scientist, you will interact with clients, regulators, and colleagues while working on fast paced and challenging environmental projects. This position will offer the right person significant opportunities for professional growth, specialized training, and leadership!

We understand that our company is our people, and our success is rooted in their professional development. We offer a flexible work schedule and ability to work remotely. We take great pride in our learning and mentoring programs, diverse, flexible, and supportive work environment, and our investment in our staff’s individual growth. We foster a culture that builds relationships based on integrity and respect, with our clients and with each other. We are a firm where everyone counts, and each employee can make a difference. Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related

jobs.title: Senior Regulatory Toxicologist (Toxicologist 3)
jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Senior Regulatory Toxicologist (Toxicologist 3)
within the Hazardous Waste and Toxics Reduction Program (HWTR).

Location:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of two days per month is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by November 18, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may be reviewed only if additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

This Senior Regulatory Toxicologist position offers a key opportunity to shape Washington’s toxics-reduction policies and advance statewide protections for human health and the environment. In this role, you will serve as the program’s senior regulatory subject matter expert, providing authoritative toxicological leadership for identifying, evaluating, and reducing threats from high-priority chemicals used in commerce. You will guide the scientific direction of the Safer Products for Washington initiative, lead complex hazard evaluations, and translate emerging toxicological research into actionable policy recommendations that support Ecology’s mission.

You will also direct the toxicology work of staff within the Toxics Awareness and Action Section and collaborate with scientific partners at the Washington Department of Health. Working closely with program leadership, you will assess the implications of emerging science, regulatory developments, and legislative proposals; communicate complex findings to technical and non-technical audiences; and help build consensus on major policy and regulatory decisions. Your work will influence statewide toxics-reduction strategies, support rulemaking and program planning, and ensure that Ecology’s actions are grounded in rigorous scientific analysis and consistent with best available science.

What You Will Do

Provide senior-level toxicological expertise and policy guidance for Ecology’s toxics-reduction initiatives, including the identification and evaluation of priority chemicals that pose the highest potential impacts to human health and the environment.
Lead the scientific framework for Safer Products for Washington by developing hazard criteria, evaluating toxicological and exposure data, and directing research to inform statewide chemical prioritization and recommended regulatory actions.
Assign, guide, and review the technical work of toxicologists within Ecology and the Washington Department of Health, ensuring scientific quality, consistency, and clarity across assessments and policy support.
Conduct and oversee toxicological assessments that identify major sources of exposure in consumer products, and provide expert recommendations for regulatory options, reporting requirements, or restrictions under Chapter 70.365 RCW.
Represent Ecology as a senior scientific expert in briefings, legislative hearings, interagency meetings, national workgroups, and public forums, communicating complex toxicological findings in clear, accessible terms.
Analyze state and federal regulatory developments, scientific literature, and emerging research to assess implications for Washington’s toxics-reduction strategy and support program decisions, bill analysis, and testimony preparation.
Develop and refine methodologies for evaluating chemical hazards and exposures, assess scientific rigor and uncertainty in studies, and adapt approaches used by federal agencies or other jurisdictions for application in Washington.
Provide toxicology support for Chemical Action Plans, product testing studies, QAPP development, regulatory implementation, and compliance activities.
Contribute to program planning and policy development by advising the Program Manager and Management Team on scientific considerations, resource needs, and long-term strategies to reduce toxic threats statewide.
Prepare and deliver presentations, workshops, and webinars; author or co-author scientific publications; and ensure that Ecology’s scientific work is broadly accessible and accurately communicated to varied audiences.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Ten (10) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Toxicology & Public Health Expertise — Ability to apply toxicology and public health knowledge to assess human and ecological health impacts resulting from exposure to priority chemicals and chemical classes, including impacts on sensitive populations and sensitive species.
Regulatory and Policy Analysis Skill in reviewing and interpreting state and federal environmental laws, rules, and scientific policy documents to inform program decisions and develop recommended regulatory actions.
Science Policy Support — Ability to identify ecological and human health risk implications of proposed legislation and regulatory developments, and to support bill analysis, testimony preparation, and agency toxics-reduction strategy.
Science Communication Ability to translate complex toxicological and scientific information into clear, accessible language for diverse technical and non-technical audiences, including agency leadership and legislators.
Technical Leadership and Work Direction Experience leading and coordinating scientific work, assigning and reviewing technical tasks, and providing expert guidance and direction to cross-disciplinary staff and interagency partners.
Hazard & Risk Framework Development — Ability to research, develop, and apply a hazard- and exposure-based framework for identifying and prioritizing chemicals of concern, distinct from a risk-assessment approach.
Research and Scientific Method Application Demonstrated competency in designing, conducting, or reviewing scientific research, evaluating uncertainties, and applying sound methodology to support hazard, exposure, or risk analyses. Ability to assess the scientific rigor, quality, uncertainty and applicability of toxicological and exposure studies to problems being addressed in Washington.
Interested Parties & Interagency Engagement — Ability to represent the program to the Legislature, other state and federal agencies, Tribes, and the public, including serving as agency liaison/spokesperson and building consensus among parties with diverse interests.

Education
: Involving a major study in toxicology, reproductive and developmental biology, or in another health or ecological related science with a major emphasis in toxicology.

Examples Of How To Qualify

10 years of experience.
9 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
8 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
7 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
6 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
4 years of experience AND a Master’s degree or above.

Desired Qualifications

Diplomat of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT) or similar certification – either existing or willingness to obtain certification.
Experience in one or more of the following disciplines: chemical hazard assessments, alternatives assessments, chemical risk evaluations, exposure assessments, health impact assessments, or green chemistry.
Experience with toxicology tools, models, and chemical data base systems (e.g. ToxCast).
Awareness or involvement with toxicology professional organizations such as the Society of Toxicology (SOT), Society of Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry (SETAC) and other professional networks.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify
system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIRis both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website .

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.

Need an Accommodation?

If you need reasonable accommodation during the application and/or screening process, including this job announcement in an alternate format:

Please contact us at 360-407-6186 and select #2 for Recruitment or email careers@ecy.wa.gov
If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 711 or 1-800-833-6384.

Questions?

For specific questions about the position location options, schedule, or duties, please contact Kimberly Grieves at Kimberly.Grieves@ecy.wa.gov
If you need assistance applying for this job, are inquiring about the status of your application, would like to request the full position description, or have any other questions, please contact the Recruitment Team at careers@ecy.wa.gov

About the Hazardous Waste and Toxics Reduction
Program

The mission of the Hazardous Waste and Toxics Reduction program is to protect Washington’s residents and environment by reducing the use of toxic chemicals, safely managing dangerous waste, preventing new contaminated sites, and cleaning up contamination .

As the State of Washington’s environmental protection agency, we are deeply committed to protecting, preserving, and enhancing Washington’s environment for current and future generations. Joining Ecology means becoming part of a team dedicated to protecti

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Aerostar Environmental and Construction LLC is growing! We are seeking talented professionals aspiring to become well rounded Environmental Scientists / Industrial Hygienists. We are committed to fostering a work environment that offers long-term stability and growth. We value our employees and are dedicated to supporting their success throughout their career with us. With a strong track record of consistent growth, we provide a secure and dependable workplace for those looking for a lasting career.

We are seeking scientists who are interested in identifying, investigating, evaluating, and assessing for elements, chemicals, and materials that could be detrimental to the environment, the public, and to workers. We also support and encourage cross-training through our business lines to promote growth in your area of expertise, not only based on your chosen educational focus and degree, but to allow opportunity for you to flourish and expand your career expectations. Our projects are located throughout, and occasionally outside, the United States which makes travel an imperative part of job expectations. Our team is looking for scientifically minded individuals seeking constant growth and constant inquisitiveness to enter into the environmental and industrial hygiene field or that are ready to accelerate to a more advanced and experienced position in the fields of environmental science, industrial hygiene, and safety and health.

Aerostar Environmental and Construction LLC offers a great benefits package complete with medical, dental, and vision insurance, health savings account health reimbursement account, flexible spending account, employer paid life and disability, 401(k) matching, and paid time off along with other essential benefits.

This position will report to our office location in Jacksonville with travel to sites nation-wide and potentially OCONUS.

The salary range for this role is $40,000-$60,000 annually.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties, but not all duties performed for this position. Other duties may be assigned.

Conduct building assessments in occupied and unoccupied buildings including occupied spaces, confined spaces, roofs, and crawl spaces
Collecting samples of multiple media including air samples, bulk samples, samples in-situ, and personal samples
Conduct oversight activities of workers and monitor and direct work practices
Maintaining certification and clearance for sensitive sites including DoD controlled facilities, child education facilities, assisted living facilities, and occupied residences and workplaces
Interaction with facility and residential occupants in a professional manner
Calculations of spatial and material square footage
Understanding, learning, interpreting, and implementing OSHA, EPA, state, and local regulations and standards
Meticulous note taking and documentation
Developing reports with unbiased observational information, laboratory analytical results, and recommendations based on regulations and industry standards

Minimum Qualifications

To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The qualifications listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

Associate’s or Bachelor's in Geology, Engineering, Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Occupational Safety and Health or related studies.
Experience in performing environmental field investigations, building assessments, industrial hygiene assessments, and/or other geoscience-related fields is a plus
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Excellent computer skills.
As a condition of employment, you may be required to pass a preemployment drug screening and have acceptable references and background check results.
Any accreditation/licensing/certification associated with asbestos, lead-based paint, radon, mold, health and safety, or worker protection
Construction experience and familiarity with building construction
40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification

Additional Qualifying Factors

As a condition of employment, you will be required to pass a pre-employment drug screening (post accepted offer) and have acceptable background check results. If applicable to the contract, you must also obtain the appropriate clearance levels required and be able to obtain access to military installations.

Necessary Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Employees must always maintain a constant state of mental alertness. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position requires the ability to maneuver around work sites, see, hear, and verbally communicate with co-workers and clients. Essential and marginal functions may require maintaining the physical condition necessary for bending, stooping, sitting, crawling, walking, or standing for prolonged periods of time; frequent opportunity to move about and to work outside the office environment for extended periods involving exposure to the elements with weather that will include extreme heat, cold, wind, rain or other inclement weather, walking over rough and uneven surfaces, and routine lifting of 35 pounds or more. If required, individual must properly use personal protective equipment (PPE) including but not limited to; hard hats, safety-toed boots, eye protection, respiratory protection, hearing protection, and fall protection. Must maintain a constant state of mental alertness at all times. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Working Conditions

Job is performed in a combination of office work, work throughout occupied and unoccupied buildings, and outdoor site locations. The office setting includes exposure to computer screens and requires extensive use of a computer, keyboard, and mouse. Building assessments will be conducted throughout buildings including crawl spaces, attic spaces, work from extreme heights, and confined spaces. Outdoor settings include walking, driving, and carrying supplies throughout all seasons with exposure to heat and cold conditions, and potentially wildlife. Is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals, and loud noise.

About Bristol Bay Construction Holdings LLC

Bristol Bay Construction Holdings LLC (BBCH) is a holding company of Bristol Bay Native Corporation, an Alaska Native Corporation. The BBCH family of companies include 8(a), small, and large businesses operating under the Aerostar, CCI, CSI, Herman, and SES brands. The vision of BBCH is to be best value companies and employers of choice, recognized for our dedication to our unity of purpose, values, employees, clients, and shareholders. For three decades, our best-value companies have provided federal and commercial clients with superior quality and cost-effective, innovative, and sustainable solutions for general construction, restoration services, civil works, fuels systems, environmental services, professional services, and facility support services.

BBCH gives lawful hiring, promotion, training, and retention preference to BBCH shareholders, shareholder descendants, and shareholder spouses who meet the minimum qualifications for the position. While preference is given to these individuals, all employment decisions are based on qualifications and business needs.

We are an equal-opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration for employment, without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, gender, or gender identity, age, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability, pregnancy or parental status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

We participate in the E-Verify Employment Verification Program. We are a drug-free workplace.

Full-time

Industries

Job Description And Duties

Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking a Environmental Scientist to evaluate vegetation management aspects of electric utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electrical Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.

Under close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) of the Environmental Policy Branch in the Environmental Science Division, the incumbent will review and evaluate vegetation management-related aspects of electric utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans, develop utility vegetation management best management practices for wildfire safety, and contribute to the development of Guidelines. The incumbent will also develop and maintain relationships with Federal, State, and local agency partners and serve as an environmental science subject matter expert to assist other Energy Safety Divisions.

The reporting location for this position is California Natural Resources Agency Building located at 715 P Street, Sacramento, CA 95814.

Experience in policy research and analysis.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Coordinator
jobs.description:
Summary

Arcadis, APM Group Inc., has an opening for an EHS Coordinator to join our team in Boise, ID.
In this field-based role you will assist in the development and continuous improvement of the Arcadis safety culture through direct on-site support, developing and conducting EHS training programs, and providing safety coaching and mentoring to the department.

Successful candidates will have a minimum of 1 year of experience in construction EHS-related work on a project site, ideally supporting semiconductor, life science, or related industrial high-tech projects. Other experience may be considered. Candidates must live within commutable distance to the project site.

Responsibilities

Act as a technical resource for construction management group on assigned project site(s).
Provide on-site safety support for construction management projects.
Review safety inspections and safety observations generated by field personnel and provide coaching to ensure continuous improvement.
Conduct EH&S training, including but not limited to orientations, topics relevant to ongoing work, and post-incident follow-up.
Conduct visits for on-site safety compliance and provide appropriate and timely feedback.
Participate in subcontractor kick-off meetings.
Participate in constructability review meetings with subcontractors.
Under supervision, review job hazard analysis (JHA).
Participate in Construction Incident Analysis Meetings.
Review and validate corrective action plan action items on site.
Daily duties include but are not limited to participating in the safety leadership team, safety coordination meetings, mass safety meetings, daily pre-task plans, daily field compliance audits.
Prepare and submit safety metrics, including leading indicators and lagging indicators, as needed per policy and team requirements.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills And Qualifications

1+ years’ construction safety experience preferred.
STS-C certification or equivalent a plus.
Semiconductor & Data Center construction experience preferred.
Bi-lingual in Spanish preferred; both written and verbal.
General understanding of current federal, state, and local safety regulations as well as industry consensus standards.
Excellent verbal, written, and communications skills.
Formal training in safety management (OSHA, formal education, or similar, or combination thereof).
Organized and efficient in time and task management.
Ability to work independently with some oversight.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Exposure to Procore, Bluebeam, and other software platforms in use.
Local candidates required. Ability to provide valid work authorization for US employment required.

Working Conditions

This field-based position will work primarily on a construction site with minimal time in an office. Environmental conditions may vary and could include, but not be limited to, hot and cold temperatures, severe/inclement weather, and other factors.
Noise levels will be high at times depending upon work location.
Must wear required PPE as required by Arcadis or host employer(s).
Due to cleanroom protocols, successful candidates may need to wear cleanroom coveralls and follow client hygiene protocols.
Frequent walking, occasional lifting of objects in excess of 20lbs, frequent standing required.

The Company

DPS Group, Inc. is proudly part of the Arcadis Group of Companies and is a global EPCM firm offering full-service solutions within the Life Sciences (pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical technology) and Advanced Technology (semiconductor, data center, and solar) industries. DPS is dedicated to delivering successful projects with a ‘client-first’ mentality and personal touch across a range of market sectors: Project and Program Management, Procurement, Design, Construction Management, Health and Safety Management, Commissioning, Qualification, and Start-up.

DPS Engineering Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and employment selection decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

At WSP, we are driven by inspiring future-ready pioneers to innovate. We are seeking an experienced Environmental Air Quality Modeler
to join our growing Environmental Team. This position offers the opportunity to work on complex air quality permitting, compliance, and modeling projects for a diverse portfolio of industrial clients throughout the United States.

This role is preferably based in our Columbus, Ohio office; however, qualified candidates may be located in any WSP office across the United States.
The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams nationwide to deliver innovative environmental solutions, support critical infrastructure and industrial development projects, and help clients navigate an evolving regulatory landscape.

The ideal candidate will bring strong technical expertise in air quality permitting and modeling, sound project management skills, and a commitment to delivering exceptional client service while helping shape sustainable outcomes for our communities and environment.

Your Impact

Lead and support air quality permitting, compliance, and regulatory projects for industrial clients.
Prepare and review New Source Review (NSR), Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD), and other air permit applications.
Conduct air dispersion modeling analyses using tools such as AERMOD and other applicable modeling platforms.
Perform emissions calculations, emissions inventories, and air regulatory analyses.
Prepare semi-annual, annual, and other regulatory compliance reports.
Interpret federal, state, and local air quality regulations and provide strategic guidance to clients.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality environmental solutions.
Manage project scopes, schedules, budgets, and deliverables while ensuring technical excellence.
Build and maintain strong client relationships through responsive communication and trusted technical support.
Support business development initiatives, including proposal preparation, client engagement, and identification of new project opportunities.
Mentor junior staff and contribute to the continued growth and development of the Air Quality practice.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Meteorology, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline.
5+ years of professional experience in air quality permitting, regulatory compliance, and environmental consulting.
Demonstrated experience with:
Air dispersion modeling.
New Source Review (NSR) permitting.
Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) permitting.
Nonattainment permitting requirements.
Air emissions inventory development.
Title V permitting.
Regulatory compliance evaluations.
Air emission control technology assessments.

Experience performing PSD modeling using AERMOD.
Strong understanding of federal and state air quality regulations, policies, and emerging regulatory programs.
Excellent technical writing, communication, data analysis, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and client relationships simultaneously.
Proven ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with both AERMOD and CALPUFF modeling platforms.
Existing professional relationships with state and federal regulatory agencies.
Experience working with the Texas, Ohio, Indiana, or Kentucky environmental regulatory agencies.
Air permitting and compliance experience within one or more of the following industries:
Utilities and Power Generation
Data Centers
Oil and Gas
Refining
Chemical Manufacturing
Industrial Manufacturing

Active participation in industry or environmental professional organizations.
Strong client management and business development experience.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate client needs and develop practical, solution-oriented recommendations.

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

Meta is seeking an Environmental Analyst to support environmental monitoring and analytics critical to regulatory compliance of our international data center and network builds. This position will work on cross-functional program efforts for the large and growing global infrastructure portfolio during the pre-development, construction, and operations phases. This position will work closely with both the data center and network environmental teams, as well as our land management team, and will report directly to the Global Head of Environment within the Site Development organization. Some travel is necessary to visit our sites (up to 25%).

Own and evolve analytical frameworks for tracking Meta's global data center, network, and land management environment obligations, including portfolio dashboards, milestone and reporting tracking, and risk indicators
Design analytical approaches spanning the full environmental permitting lifecycle—integrating data from site selection, permitting, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
Own the analytical data architecture for the environmental and land management team to inform reporting across multiple environmental disciplines (air, noise, cultural, biology, native habitat, contaminants, etc)
Drive automation of data collection, quality control/assurance, transformation, and reporting workflows to reduce manual effort and support compliance with environmental regulations and permits
Serve as an analytical integration point for stakeholders with the environmental and land management team
Design and document analytical methodologies, SOPs, and training materials that enable partners to self-serve for routine data needs

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field
5+ years of experience in analytics, strategy, or environmental programs
Experience in designing analytical frameworks and executing complex multi-variable analyses independently
Experience building portfolio-level dashboards and reporting systems that drive executive decision-making
Experience communicating complex analytical findings to leadership and cross-functional partners through presentations, reports, or executive summaries
Proficiency in SQL, Python, or R for data manipulation and environmental data pipeline development, combined with experience in Tableau or Power BI for visualization

Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize analytical workflows and drive measurable improvements in data quality, reporting efficiency, or decision-support speed
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)

Familiarity with hyperscale data center development lifecycle phases, including site selection, environmental permitting, entitlement, and construction

jobs.description:
Why RTI:

RTI International is an independent, scientific research institute dedicated to improving the human condition. Our vision is to address the world's most critical problems with technical and science-based solutions in pursuit of a better future. Clients rely on us to answer questions that demand an objective and multidisciplinary approach—one that integrates expertise across social, statistical, data, and laboratory sciences, engineering, and other technical disciplines to solve the world’s most challenging problems.  
  
We believe in the promise of science and technical solutions, and we push ourselves every day to deliver on that promise for the good of people, communities, and businesses in the US and around the world. If you are looking for the opportunity to make a real difference, RTI is the place for you.

About the Hiring Group:

Are you passionate about water resources and environmental science? RTI’s Water, Agriculture, Natural Resources, and Energy Solutions (WARES) Group is seeking a motivated Research Environmental Scientist to join our hydromet and flood risk team. We develop innovative tools and analytical methods that support hydropower owners, dam safety programs, and the broader water resources community.

Our team is recognized for expertise in precipitation frequency analysis and probable flood hazard assessments (PFHA). As a nonprofit research institute, RTI also supports internal R&D to drive innovation and create real-world impact.

As part of the team, you will contribute to a broad range of meteorological frequency analyses and extreme storm analyses. Candidates should be able to demonstrate experience or exposure in several of the areas listed below (not all are required).

**Why Join Us?**

* Work on impactful domestic and international water resources projects.
* Apply state-of-the-art computational tools to complex water management challenges.
* Help advance modeling technologies and analytical methods.
* Collaborate with leading experts in a supportive, multidisciplinary environment.
* This position can be either based in RTI’s U.S. office in Research Triangle Park, NC, or it can be fully remote. Teleworking is permitted within the United States only.

What You'll Do:

You will support project teams requiring meteorological expertise to support hydrologic hazards, flood forecasting, and other analyses. You will work daily using scripts, tools, and techniques to efficiently prepare and analyze meteorological data including addressing climate change impacts using GCM data. You will also support project management and grow project portfolios.

**Essential Duties:**

* Collaborate with the Hydromet team to implement and enhance RTI’s hydrometeorological analysis tools.
* Perform data processing, quality control, and automation using scripts and tools.
* Collect, process, quality control, and statistically analyze large datasets of meteorological information.
* Develop code to improve existing hydrometeorological analysis tools and link to other existing hydrologic modeling or forecasting tools.
* Contribute to precipitation frequency and probable maximum precipitation analyses in support of dam safety projects.
* Lead small projects or task orders of moderate complexity.
* Contribute to proposal development.
* Share work internally and externally through presentations and conference papers.
* Make informed decisions based on data, best practices, and team input.
* Support business development by identifying opportunities to expand or enhance existing projects and developing research ideas or white papers.

What You'll Need:

**Minimum Education & Experience:**

Bachelor’s degree [DM1] and 8 years of relevant experience, master’s degree and 6 years of relevant experience, or a PhD and 1 year of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Relevant fields include Meteorology, Atmospheric Science, Hydrology, Climate Studies, or a related discipline.

**Minimum Required Qualifications:**

* Experience in the following areas:
  + Statistical analysis of hydrometeorological time series, precipitation frequency, and probable maximum precipitation.
  + Collection, QA/QC, and interpretation of hydrometeorological data.
  + Technical documentation and report writing.
  + Experience working with meteorological GIS datasets.
  + Proficiency with open-source programming languages (Python, R, C#, VB.NET) for data management, transformation, QC, and statistical analysis.
  + Basic geospatial processing and mapping using ArcGIS or QGIS.
  + Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and familiarity with relational databases (SQL).
* To qualify, applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States and should not require, now or in the future, sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B visa status, etc.).

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with GCM datasets.
* Experience with extreme storm analyses.
* Familiarity with probabilistic or stochastic modeling concepts.

This is a hands-on, lab-based leadership role.*

  

**Position Description**

**The Opportunity**

Nurix Therapeutics is seeking a Head of Investigative Toxicology to establish and lead our in-house in vitro toxicology testing capability. Reporting into the Preclinical Toxicology leadership team, this individual will build the assays, infrastructure, and mechanistic understanding needed to characterize target- and modality-related safety liabilities earlier in discovery, reducing reliance on external CROs for early screening and de-risking. This is a hands-on, lab-based leadership role for a scientist who wants to build a function from the ground up, working in close partnership with Discovery Biology, Chemistry, DMPK, and Pharmacology to inform lead selection and optimization for our growing pipeline of targeted protein degrader programs. The position reports to the Senior Vice President, Nonclinical Toxicology.

***In Vitro Toxicology Capability Build***

* Define the technical roadmap and prioritize which in vitro assays to bring in-house versus continue to source through CRO partners, balancing scientific value, cost, and speed
* Own day-to-day lab operations for the function, including equipment maintenance, vendor and reagent management, and data management systems

* Serve as the in vitro/investigative toxicology representative on discovery project teams, providing mechanistic insight into target and modality-related safety findings

* Partner with DMPK, Pharmacology, and Discovery Biology to integrate in vitro toxicology data into candidate selection, structure-activity relationship (SAR), and lead optimization decisions
* Translate in vitro findings into risk assessments and clear recommendations for project teams and research leadership

* Represent in vitro/investigative toxicology in Research Leadership meetings and contribute to the broader nonclinical safety strategy
* Foster a collaborative, science-driven culture consistent with Nurix's values of rigor, creativity, and patient focus

* PhD in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Molecular Biology, or a closely related life sciences discipline; postdoctoral training preferred
* 10+ years of relevant nonclinical safety, investigative toxicology, or molecular/cellular toxicology experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including direct, hands-on laboratory experience with in vitro and/or complex in vitro (MPS) model systems
* Demonstrated experience building, validating, and implementing new in vitro assay platforms or laboratory capabilities in an industry setting
* Strong working knowledge of mechanisms of drug-induced toxicity and the in vitro tools used to investigate them (e.g., high content imaging, primary and immortalized cell culture, hepatocyte/cardiomyocyte models, genotoxicity assays)

* Experience managing CRO relationships and evaluating build-versus-buy decisions for laboratory capabilities

* Experience with targeted protein degradation (TPD) or other novel small molecule modalities, including neosubstrate/off-target degradation risk assessment
* Experience establishing or scaling a laboratory function within a growing, clinical-stage biotech
* Familiarity with New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and organ-on-chip/microphysiological systems
* People management or mentoring experience
* Strong publication record in investigative or molecular toxicology
